translations.text: Blessed is the man who does not follow the counsel of the ungodly, or stand in the way of sinners, or sit in the seat of those who destroy.
Instead, his delight is in the law of the Lord, and he meditates on his law day and night.
He will be like a tree planted beside streams of water, which gives its fruit in its season. Its leaf will not fall, and everything he does will prosper.
Not so the ungodly! They are like dust which the wind [?] from the face of the earth.
And the ungodly will not rise [?], nor sinners [?] the righteous.
For [?] the Lord [?] the way of the righteous [?], and the way of the ungodly [?].
Why did the nations [?] rage, and the peoples meditate on empty things?
The kings of the earth took their stand, and the rulers gathered together against the Lord and against his Anointed One.
Let us tear apart their bonds and throw off their yoke from us.
He who lives in heaven will laugh at them, and the Lord will mock them.
Then he will speak to them in his anger and terrify them in his wrath.
But I have been appointed king by him over Zion, his holy mountain,
proclaiming the Lord’s decree. The Lord said to me, “You are my Son; today I have begotten you.
Ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance, and the ends of the earth as your possession.
You will shepherd them with an iron rod; you will shatter them like a potter’s vessel.”
And now, kings, understand; accept instruction, all you who judge the earth.
Serve the Lord with fear, and rejoice in him with trembling.
Accept instruction, lest the Lord become angry and you perish from the righteous way. When his wrath flares up suddenly, blessed are all who trust in [?].
A Psalm of David.
Lord, why have those who trouble me multiplied? Many rise up against me.
Many say of my soul, “There is no salvation for him in his God.”
But you, Lord, are my protector, my glory, and you have lifted up my head.
With my voice I cried out to the Lord, and he heard me from his holy mountain.
I fell asleep and slept, and I arose, for the Lord will protect me.
I will not fear myriads of people who attack me all around [?].
Rise up, Lord! Save me, my God! For you have struck all who were hostile to me without cause; you have broken the teeth of sinners.
Salvation belongs to the Lord, and your blessing is upon your people.
When I called, you heard me, God of my righteousness. In distress you gave me room. Have mercy on me; hear my [?].
Children of men, how long will you be hard-hearted? Why do you love emptiness and seek falsehood?
Know that the Lord has made his faithful one wondrous. The Lord will hear me when I call to him.
Be angry, but do not sin. For what you say in your hearts, be remorseful on your beds.
Offer a sacrifice of righteousness, and put your trust in the Lord.
Many say, “Who will show us good things?” The light of your face has been marked upon us, Lord.
You have put gladness in my heart. They have grown rich from the yield of their wheat, wine, and oil.
In peace I will fall asleep and rest, for you, Lord, have made me dwell alone in hope.
A Psalm of David.
Listen to my words, Lord; understand my cry.
Attend to the sound of my prayer, my King and my God, for to you I will pray, Lord.
In the morning you will hear my voice; in the morning I will stand before you and watch.
For you are not a God who desires lawlessness; the wicked will not dwell with you.
Nor will lawbreakers stand before your eyes. You have hated all who practice lawlessness.
You will destroy all who speak lies. The Lord abhors a bloodthirsty and deceitful man.
But through the abundance of your mercy I will enter your house, and in fear of you I will bow down toward your holy temple.
Lord, lead me in your righteousness. Because of my enemies, make my path straight before you.
For there is no truth in their mouths; their hearts are empty. Their throats are open graves; with their tongues they practiced deceit.
Judge them, God. Let them fall through their own schemes. Cast them out for their many wicked deeds, for they have provoked you to anger, Lord.
Let all who trust in you rejoice. They will rejoice forever, and you will dwell among them. Those who love your name will boast in you.
For you will bless the righteous, Lord. You have crowned us with favor as with a shield.
A Psalm of David.
Lord, do not rebuke me in your fury or discipline me in your anger.
Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am weak; heal me, Lord, for my bones are shaken.
My soul is also deeply troubled; and you, Lord—how long [?]
Turn back, Lord, and deliver my soul [?]; save me for the sake of your mercy.
For in death no one remembers you; and in Hades who will give you thanks?
I am worn out with my groaning; every night I wash my bed and soak my bedding with my tears.
My eye is troubled by anger; I have grown old among all my enemies.
Depart from me, all you who practice lawlessness, for the Lord has heard the sound of my weeping.
The Lord has heard my prayer; the Lord has accepted my plea.
May all my enemies be ashamed and troubled; may they turn back and be utterly put to shame very soon.
A Psalm of David. Glory.
Lord my God, I have put my trust in you; save me from all who pursue me, and deliver me.
Otherwise he may seize my soul like a lion, with no one to deliver or save me.
Lord my God, if I have done this, if [?] there is injustice in my hands,
if I have repaid those who repay me with evil, may I fall away from my enemies empty-handed.
Then let the enemy pursue my soul and overtake it; let him trample my life into the ground and lay my glory in the dust.
Arise, Lord, in your anger; rise up at the boundaries of your enemies. And arise, Lord my God, by your command [?] which you gave.
And an assembly of peoples will surround you; and for its sake he will return to the heights [?].
The Lord judges the peoples. Judge me, Lord, according to my righteousness and according to the innocence within me.
May the wickedness of sinners come to an end; you will establish the righteous, testing hearts and inward parts, O God,
who are righteous. My help comes from God, who saves the upright in heart.
God is a righteous judge, mighty and patient, and does not bring down anger every day.
If he does not turn back, he will sharpen his sword; he has drawn his bow and made it ready.
And on it he has prepared weapons of death; he has made his arrows for those who burn.
Look, he labored to give birth to injustice; he conceived trouble and gave birth to lawlessness.
He dug a pit and hollowed it out, and he will fall into the hole he made.
His trouble will return upon his own head, and his wrongdoing will come down upon his crown.
I will give thanks to the Lord for his righteousness, and I will sing to the name of the Lord Most High.
A psalm of David.
O Lord, our Lord, how wonderful is your name throughout the earth! For your majesty has been raised above the heavens.
From the mouths of infants at the breast you have perfected praise, because of your enemies, to destroy the enemy and the avenger.
For they will see the heavens, the work of your fingers, the moon and the stars that you established.
What is man, that you remember him, or the son of man, that you care for him?
You made him a little lower than the angels; you crowned us with glory and honor.
And you set him over the works of his hands. He will put all things under his feet:
all sheep and oxen, and also the beasts of the field,
and the birds of heaven, and the fish of the sea that travel the paths of the seas.
O Lord, our Lord, how wonderful is your name throughout the earth!
Glory. Sessional hymn. For the end, concerning the hidden things of the Son. A psalm of David.
I will give thanks to you, O Lord, with all my heart; I will recount all your wonders.
I will be glad and rejoice in you, and I will sing to your name, O Most High.
When my enemy turns back, they will grow weak and perish before your face.
For you have upheld my judgment and my cause, sitting on the throne, judging righteously.
You rebuked the nations; the ungodly man perished. His name will be erased forever and ever.
The enemy’s weapons have utterly failed, and you have destroyed the city. Their memory has perished with a crash,
but the Lord remains forever. He has prepared his throne for judgment,
and he will judge the world in righteousness; he will judge the peoples fairly.
And the Lord became a refuge for the poor, a helper at the right time in distress.
And let those who know your name trust in you, for you have not abandoned those who seek you, O Lord.
Sing to the Lord who dwells in Zion; proclaim his deeds among the nations.
For he who avenges blood remembered them; he did not forget the cry of the poor.
Have mercy on me, Lord; see my humiliation at the hands of my enemies, you who lift me up from the gates of death.
So that I may proclaim all your praises at the gates of the daughter of Zion. Let us rejoice in your salvation.
The nations have sunk into the pit they made; their foot has been caught in the net they hid.
The Lord is known by the judgments he carries out; the sinner has been caught in the works of his own hands.
Sinners will return to Hades—all the nations that forget God.
For the needy will not be forgotten forever; the patient endurance of the poor will not perish forever.
Arise, Lord; do not let a mortal prevail. Let the nations be judged before you.
Appoint a lawgiver over them, Lord, so that the nations may understand that they are mortals.
Why, Lord, do you stand far away and look away at times of need, in affliction?
In the arrogance of the wicked, the poor man is set ablaze; they are caught in the schemes they devise.
For the sinner is praised for the desires of his soul, and the oppressor is blessed.
The sinner has provoked the Lord; in the greatness of his anger he will not seek. God is not before his eyes.
His ways are defiled at all times. Your judgments are removed from his sight; he overcomes all my enemies.
For he said in his heart, “I will not be shaken; from generation to generation I will be free from harm.”
His mouth is full of cursing, bitterness, and deceit; under his tongue are trouble and suffering.
He sits in [?] with the rich, in secret places, to kill the innocent. His eyes watch the poor man.
He lies in wait in secret places like a lion in its enclosure. He lies in wait to seize the needy, to seize the poor man and drag him away.
Having brought him low in his net, he will bend down and fall when he has prevailed over the poor.
For he said in his heart, “God has forgotten; he has turned his face away so that he will never see.”
Arise, Lord my God; let your hand be lifted up. Do not forget your poor forever.
Why has the wicked man provoked God? For he said in his heart, “He will not call me to account.”
You see, for you observe suffering and rage, so that he may be delivered into your hands. To you I, a poor man, have been left; be a helper to the orphan.
Break the arm of the sinful and evil man; his sin will be sought out and will not be found.
The Lord is king forever and ever. You nations will perish from his land.
The Lord has heard the desire; your ear has attended to the readiness of their hearts.
To give justice to the orphan and the humble, so that man on earth may no longer exalt himself.
A PSALM OF DAVID.
I have put my trust in the Lord. How can you say to my soul, “Fly away to the mountains like a bird”?
For look, sinners have drawn their bow; they have prepared arrows in the quiver to shoot in the darkness at the upright in heart.
For they have destroyed what you accomplished. But what has the righteous person done?
The Lord is in his holy temple; the Lord has established his throne [?] in heaven. His eyes look upon the poor; his eyelids examine the children of men.
The Lord examines the righteous and the ungodly, but whoever loves injustice hates his own soul.
He will rain a snare upon sinners; fire, sulfur, and a stormy wind will be the portion of their cup.
For the Lord is righteous and has loved righteousness; his face has seen what is upright. GLORY.
FOR THE EIGHTH DAY. A PSALM OF DAVID.
Save me, Lord, for the godly person is no more, and truth has dwindled among the children of men.
Each person spoke empty things to his neighbor; with deceitful lips and a double heart they spoke evil.
The Lord will destroy all deceitful lips and the boastful tongue,
those who say, “We will exalt our tongues. Our lips are our own; who is lord over us?”
“Because of the suffering of the poor and the sighing of the needy, I will now arise,” says the Lord. “I will set myself to bringing salvation and will not hesitate over it.”
The words of the Lord are pure words: silver heated and tested in the earth, purified seven times.
You, Lord, will preserve us and protect us from this generation forever.
The ungodly walk all around; according to your greatness you have multiplied the children of men.
A PSALM OF DAVID.
How long, Lord, will you forget me—forever? How long will you turn your face away from me?
How long must I make plans within my soul, with sorrow in my heart day and night? How long will my enemy exalt himself over me?
Look upon me and hear me, Lord my God. Give light to my eyes, lest I fall asleep in death,
lest my enemy say, “I have overcome him.” Those who afflict me will rejoice if I falter.
But I have trusted in your mercy; my heart will rejoice in your salvation. I will sing to the Lord, who has done good to me, and I will sing praise to the name of the Lord Most High.
A PSALM OF DAVID.
The fool has said in his heart, “There is no God.” They have become corrupt and repulsive in their deeds, and there is no one who does good.
The Lord looked down from heaven upon humankind to see whether there was anyone who understood or sought God.
They have all turned aside; together they have become worthless. There is no one who does good, not even one.
Do none of those who practice lawlessness understand? They devour my people instead of bread and have not called upon the Lord.
There they were terrified by anguish where there was no anguish, for the Lord is among the righteous.
You have shamed the counsel of the poor, but the Lord is his hope.
Who will bring Israel’s salvation from Zion? When the Lord brings his people back from captivity, Jacob will rejoice and Israel will be glad. Glory.
A PSALM OF DAVID.
Lord, who will dwell in your dwelling place? Who will live on your holy mountain?
One who walks blamelessly, does what is right, and speaks truth in his heart;
who has not deceived with his tongue, has done no evil to his neighbor, and has accepted no reproach against those close to him.
The wicked person is despised in his sight, but he honors those who fear the Lord. He swears an oath to his neighbor and does not go back on it.
He does not lend his money at interest or accept bribes against the innocent. Whoever does these things will never be shaken.
[?] OF DAVID.
Preserve me, Lord, for I have put my hope in you.
I said to the Lord, “You are my Lord, for you have no need of my good things.”
As for the saints who are in his land, he has made all his desires wondrous among them.
Their infirmities multiplied; afterward they hurried. I will not gather their assemblies of blood, nor will I mention their names with my lips.
The Lord is the share of my inheritance and my cup; you are the one who secures my inheritance for me.
The measuring lines have fallen for me in strong places; indeed, my inheritance is secure for me.
I will bless the Lord who has given me understanding; even into the night my inward parts have instructed me.
I have always kept the Lord before me, for he is at my right hand, so that I will not be shaken.
Therefore my heart will rejoice, and my flesh too will dwell in hope.
For you will not abandon my soul in Hades, nor will you let your holy one [?] see decay.
You have made known to me the paths of life; you will fill me with joy in your presence. Beauty is at your right hand forever.
For the end. A psalm of David.
Hear my righteous cause, Lord; attend to my prayer. Listen to my supplication, which does not come from deceitful lips.
Let my judgment come from your presence; let my eyes see what is right.
You have tested my heart; you have visited me by night. You have refined me, and no wrongdoing was found in me.
Let my mouth not speak of human deeds. Because of the words of your lips, I have kept to difficult paths.
You have made my footsteps firm in your paths, so that my feet will not slip.
I cried out because God heard me. Incline your ear to me and hear my words.
Show your marvelous mercies, you who save those who trust in you from those who oppose your right hand.
And guard me, Lord, like the pupil of an eye. You will shelter me beneath the covering of your wings
from the presence of the wicked who have oppressed me. My enemies have seized my soul.
They have enclosed themselves in their own fat; their mouths have spoken arrogantly.
Those who pursue me have now surrounded me. They have fixed their eyes on casting me down to the ground.
He surrounded me like a lion ready for the hunt, and like a young lion dwelling in its hiding places.
Rise, Lord; confront them and [?]. Deliver my soul from the wicked, [?] your weapon, from the enemies of your hand.

Lord, separate them from the few on earth during their lifetime. Their bellies have been filled with your hidden things. They have had their fill of sons and have left the remainder to their little children.
But I will appear before your face in righteousness; I will be satisfied when your glory appears to me.

Glory. Sitting. For the end. For David, the servant of God, who spoke to the Lord the words of this song on the day when the Lord delivered him from the hand of his enemies; from the hand of his enemies, he said: [?]
I will love you, Lord, my strength.
The Lord is my stronghold, my refuge, and my deliverer. My God is my helper; I trust in him. He is my defender, the horn of my salvation, and my protector.
With praise I will call upon the Lord, and I will be saved from my enemies.
The pains of death gripped me, and torrents of lawlessness troubled me.
The pains of Hades surrounded me; the snares of death confronted me.
In my distress I called upon the Lord and cried out to my God. He heard my voice from his holy temple, and my cry before him will enter his ears.
The earth shook and trembled, and the foundations of the mountains were shaken. They moved because God was angry with them.
Smoke rose in his anger, and fire will flare up before his face. Coals were kindled by him.
And he bent the heavens and came down, and thick darkness was beneath his feet.
And he mounted a cherub and flew; he flew on the wings of the wind.
And he made darkness his hiding place; his shelter surrounded him: dark water in the clouds of the air.
From the brightness before him the clouds passed by, with hail and coals of fire.
And the Lord thundered [?] from heaven, and the Most High gave his voice.
He sent out arrows and scattered them; he multiplied lightning flashes and threw them into confusion.
And the springs of water appeared, and the foundations of the world were laid bare at your rebuke, Lord, at the blast of your angry breath.
He sent from on high and took hold of me; he drew me out of many waters.
He will deliver me from my strong enemies and from those who hate me, for they became stronger than I.
They confronted me on the day of my distress, and the Lord became my support.
And he brought me out into a broad place. He delivered me because he delighted in me.
And the Lord will repay me according to my righteousness, and according to the cleanness of my hands he will repay me.
For I have kept the ways of the Lord and have not acted wickedly against my God.
For all his judgments are before me, and his decrees have not departed from me.
And I will be blameless with him, and I will keep myself from my lawlessness.
And the Lord will repay me according to my righteousness and according to the cleanness of my hands before his eyes.
With the faithful you will be faithful, and with the innocent man you will be innocent.
And with the chosen you will be chosen, and with the crooked you will act crookedly.
For you will save humble people, and you will bring down the eyes of the proud.
For you light my lamp, Lord; my God, you light up my darkness.
For through you I will escape adversity, and with my God I will climb over a wall.
My God—his way is blameless; the words of the Lord are refined by fire. He is a defender of all who trust in him.
For who is God besides the Lord? Or who is God besides our God?
God clothed me with strength and made my way blameless.
He makes my feet like a deer’s and sets me on high places.
He trains my hands for battle and has placed a bronze bow on my arm.
You have given me the protection of your salvation, and your right hand has held me. Your discipline has set me completely right, and through your discipline you yourself will teach me.
You have made room for my steps beneath me, and my ankles have grown weak.
I will pursue my enemies and overtake them, and I will not turn back until they are destroyed.
I will crush them, and they will be unable to stand; they will fall beneath my feet.
You have girded me with strength for battle; you have brought down beneath me all who rise against me.
You have made my enemies turn their backs to me and put those who hate me to shame.
They cried out, and there was someone to save them; they cried to the Lord, and he did not hear them.
I will grind them fine like dust before the wind; I will wipe them away like mud in the streets.
Deliver me from the disputes of the people; you will make me head over the nations. Foreign people whom I did not know served me,
and obeyed me as soon as they heard me. Foreigners lied to me;
foreigners grew feeble and limped away from their paths.
The Lord lives, and blessed is my God! May the God of my salvation be exalted.
God gives me vengeance and has tormented peoples beneath me.
He is my deliverer from my angry enemies. You will raise me above those who rise against me; deliver me from the unjust man.
For this reason I will praise you among the nations, Lord, and sing to your name.
He makes great the salvation of the king [?] and shows mercy to his anointed, to David and his descendants forever.
Glory. For the end. A psalm of David.
The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of his hands.
Day pours out speech to day, and night proclaims knowledge to night.
For there are no speeches or words whose voices are not (not) heard.
Their proclamation has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the inhabited world. He has placed his dwelling in the sun,
and it is like [?] coming out of its bridal chamber. It will rejoice like a giant running its course.
Its rising is from one end of heaven, and its course reaches to the other end of heaven; no one can hide from its heat.
The law of the Lord is blameless, restoring souls; the testimony of the Lord is trustworthy, making little children wise.
The Lord’s ordinances are right, gladdening hearts; the Lord’s commandment enlightens the eyes from afar.
The fear of the Lord endures forever and ever; the Lord’s judgments are true and altogether righteous.
They are more desirable than gold and many precious stones, and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb.
For your servant keeps them; in keeping them there is great reward.
Who can discern their sins? Cleanse me from my hidden faults,
and spare your servant from those of others. If they do not overpower me, then I will be blameless, and I will be cleansed from great sin.
And the words of my lips and the meditation of my heart will always be pleasing before you, O Lord, my helper and my deliverer.
For the end. A psalm of David.
May the Lord hear you on the day of trouble; may the name of the God of Jacob protect you.
May he send you help from the sanctuary and defend you from Zion.
May he remember every sacrifice of yours, and may your whole burnt offerings be rich.
Give to me, O Lord, according to your heart, and fulfill your entire plan.
We will rejoice in your salvation, and in the name of the Lord our God we will [?] exalt ourselves. May the Lord fulfill all your requests.
Now I know that the Lord has saved his anointed. He will hear him from his holy heaven, with the mighty acts of his salvation.
Some rely on weapons, others on horses, but we will call on the name of the Lord our God.
They stumbled and fell, but we rose and stood upright.
O Lord, save the king, and hear us on whatever day we call on you.
For the end. A psalm of David.
O Lord, the heart will rejoice in your strength, and will rejoice greatly in your salvation.
You have given him his heart’s desire, and you have deprived him of the wish of his lips.
For you met him with the blessing of your goodness; you placed on his head a crown made from the stone of his city.
He asked you for life, and you gave it to him: length of days forever and ever.
His glory is great through your salvation; you will bestow glory and majesty on him.
For you will give him a blessing forever and ever; you will gladden him with joy in your presence.
For the king trusts in the Lord, and through the mercy of the Most High he will not be shaken.
May your hand find all your enemies; may your right hand find all who hate you.
You will make them like a fiery furnace when you appear. Lord, in your anger he will throw them into confusion, and fire will devour them.
You will destroy their offspring from the earth and their descendants from among humankind.
For they directed evil against you; they devised a plan that they will not be able to carry out.
For you will make them turn their backs; with what you have left, you will take aim at their faces.
Rise up, Lord, in your strength; we will sing and praise your power.
For the end. A psalm of David. Glory.
God, God, [?], why have you forsaken me? The words of my sinful failings are far from my salvation.
My God, I will cry out by day, and you will not hear, and by night, and it will not be counted as foolishness on my part.
But you dwell in the holy place, the praise of Israel.
Our fathers trusted in you; they trusted, and you delivered them.
They cried out to you and were saved [?]; they trusted in you and were not put to shame.
But I am a worm and not a man, mocked by people and despised by the people.
All who see me mock me; they speak with their lips and shake their heads.
He trusted in the Lord; let him deliver him. Let him save him, since he delights in him.
For you are the one who drew me out of the womb, my hope from my mother's breasts.
I have been cast upon you from the womb; from my mother's womb and belly you have been my God.
Do not withdraw from me, for trouble is near, and there is no one to help.
Many calves have surrounded me; fat young bulls [?] have hemmed me in.
They have opened their mouths against me like a lion seizing its prey and roaring.
I have been poured out like water, and all my bones have come apart. My heart has become like wax melting within my belly.
My strength has dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue has stuck to my throat, and you have brought me down into the dust of death.
For many dogs have surrounded me; a gathering of evildoers has encircled me. They nailed my hands and my feet.
All my bones were counted. They watched and stared at me.
They divided my clothes among themselves and cast lots for my garment.
But you, Lord, do not keep your help far from me; look to my defense.
Deliver my soul from the sword, my only life from the power of the dog.
Save me from the mouths of lions, and my lowliness from the horns of wild oxen.
I will proclaim your name to my brothers; in the midst of the assembly I will sing your praise.
You who fear the Lord, praise him! All you descendants of Jacob, glorify him! Let all the descendants of Israel fear him.
For he has neither despised nor rejected the prayer of the poor, nor has he turned his face away from me. When I cried out to him, he heard me.
My praise comes from you; in the great assembly I will give thanks to you. I will fulfill my vows before those who fear him.
The poor will eat and be satisfied, and those who seek the Lord will praise him. Their hearts will live forever and ever.
All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the Lord, and all the families of the nations will bow down before him.
For the kingdom belongs to the Lord, and he rules over the nations.
All the prosperous people of the earth ate and bowed down; all who go down into the earth will fall before him. And my soul lives for him.
And my descendants will serve him. A coming generation will proclaim it to the Lord,
and they will proclaim his righteousness to people yet to be born, whom the Lord has made.
A Psalm of David.
The Lord shepherds me, and he will deprive me of nothing.
He settled me in a place of pasture; beside restful waters he nourished me.
He restored my soul; he has guided me along righteous [?] for his name’s sake.
For even if I walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, because you are with me. Your rod and your staff have comforted me.
You have prepared a table before me, [?] those who afflict me. You have anointed my head with oil, and your cup that makes me drunk—how powerful it is!
And your mercy will pursue me all the days of my life, and may I dwell in the house of the Lord for many days.
A Psalm of David.
The earth belongs to the Lord, and everything that fills it, the inhabited world and all who live in it.
He founded it upon the seas and established it upon the rivers.
Who will ascend the mountain of the Lord, or who will stand in his holy place?
One whose hands are innocent and whose heart is pure, who has not devoted his soul to vanity and has not sworn deceitfully to his neighbor.
He will receive a blessing from the Lord and mercy from God his Savior.
This is the generation of those who seek the Lord, who seek the face of the God of Jacob.
Be lifted up, you everlasting gates, and the King of glory will come in.
Who is this King of glory? The Lord, strong and mighty, the Lord, mighty in battle.
Lift up your gates, you rulers, and be lifted up, you everlasting gates, and the King of glory will come in.
Who is this King of glory? The Lord of hosts—he is [?] the King of glory.
A psalm of David. Glory. [?]
To you, Lord, I have lifted up my soul, my God.
In you I have trusted; let me never be put to shame. Do not let my enemies laugh at me.
For none who wait for you will be put to shame. Let those who act lawlessly without cause be put to shame.
Show me your ways, Lord, and teach me your paths.
Guide me in your truth and teach me, for you are God my Savior, and I have waited for you all day long.
Remember your compassion, Lord, and your mercies, for they are from everlasting.
Do not remember the sins of my youth or my ignorance. In your mercy remember me, for the sake of your goodness, Lord.
The Lord is good and upright. Therefore he will give sinners instruction in the way.
He will guide the meek in justice; he will teach the meek his ways.
All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth for those who seek his covenant and his testimonies.
For your name’s sake, Lord, forgive my sin, for it is great.
Who is the man who fears the Lord? He will give him instruction [?] in the way he chooses.
His soul will dwell among good things, and his descendants will inherit the earth.
The Lord is the strength of those who fear him, and he will reveal his covenant to them.
My eyes are always toward the Lord, for he will pull my feet out of the net.
Look upon me and have mercy on me, for I am alone and poor.
The troubles of my heart have multiplied; bring me out of my many distresses.
See my lowliness and my suffering, and forgive all my sins.
See my enemies, how they have multiplied, and how they hate me with unjust hatred.
Guard my soul and deliver me. Do not let me be put to shame, for I have trusted in you.
The innocent and upright have clung to me, for I have waited for you, Lord.
Deliver Israel, O God, from all his troubles.
A Psalm of David.
Judge me, Lord, for I have walked in my innocence. I have trusted in the Lord, and I will not falter.
Test me, Lord, and examine me. Refine my innermost being and my heart with fire.
For your mercy is before my eyes, and I have lived pleasingly in your truth.
I have not sat with an assembly devoted to vanity, and I will not go in with lawbreakers.
I have hated the assembly of evildoers, and I will not sit with the ungodly.
I will wash my hands among the innocent and walk around your altar, Lord,
so that I may hear a voice and your praise. I will proclaim all your wonders.
Lord, I have loved the beauty of your house and the place where your glory dwells.
Do not destroy my soul with the ungodly, or my life with bloodthirsty men,
in whose hands are lawless deeds, and whose right hand is filled with bribes. [?]
But I ([?]) have walked in my innocence. Deliver me, Lord, and have mercy on me.
My foot stands on upright ground. In the assemblies I will bless you, Lord.
Of David. Before the anointing.
The Lord is my light and my savior; whom shall I fear? The Lord is the defender of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
When evildoers draw near to devour my flesh, my enemies who afflict me will falter and fall.
If an army encamps against me, my heart will not fear. If war rises against me, I will trust in him.
One thing I have asked of the Lord, and this I will seek: to dwell in the Lord’s house all the days of my life, to behold the Lord’s beauty and visit his holy temple.
For he hid me in his shelter on the day of my trouble. He concealed me in the secret place of his shelter; he raised me upon a rock.
And now, behold, he has raised my head above my enemies around me, and I have offered in his shelter a sacrifice of praise and joyful shouting. I sing and will sing praises to the Lord.
Hear, Lord, my voice with which I have cried out. Have mercy on me and hear me.
My heart said to you, “I will seek the Lord.” My face has sought you; your face, Lord, I will seek.
Do not turn your face away from me, and do not turn away in anger from your servant. Be my helper; do not reject me or abandon me, O God my Savior.
For my father and my mother have abandoned me, but the Lord has taken me in.
Make your way a law for me, Lord, and lead me along a straight path because of my enemies.
Do not hand me over to those who oppress me, for false witnesses have risen against me, and falsehood has lied to itself.
I believe that I will see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living.
Wait for the Lord; be courageous, and let my heart be strong. Wait for the Lord.
Glory. A psalm of David.
To you, Lord, I will cry. My God, do not be silent toward me, lest, if you are silent toward me, I become like those who go down into the pit.
Hear, Lord, the voice of my prayer when I pray to you, when I lift up my hands toward your holy temple.
Do not drag me away with sinners, and do not destroy me with those who do wrong, who speak peace to their neighbors while evil is in their hearts.
Give them, Lord, according to their deeds and according to the evil of their undertakings. Give them according to the works of their hands; repay (repay) them what they deserve.
Because they have not understood the deeds of the Lord or the work of his hands, you will tear them down and will not build them up.
Blessed is the Lord, for he has heard the voice of my prayer.
The Lord is my helper and my deliverer. My heart trusted in him, and he became my helper, and my flesh flourished. I will willingly give thanks to him.
The Lord is strength for his people and the saving defender of his anointed.
Save your people, Lord, and bless your inheritance; save them and lift them up forever.
A psalm of David. For the departure [?].
Bring to the Lord, O sons of God; bring to the Lord young rams. Bring to the Lord glory and honor.
Bring to the Lord the glory of his name. Bow down before the Lord in his holy court.
The voice of the Lord is over the waters. The God of glory has thundered; the Lord is over the mighty waters.
The voice of the Lord is powerful; the voice of the Lord is majestic.
The voice of the Lord shatters cedars, and the Lord will shatter the cedars of Lebanon.
He will grind them fine like the calf of Lebanon, and his beloved one is like a young wild ox.
The voice of the Lord splits the flame of fire.
The voice of the Lord shakes the wilderness; the Lord will shake the wilderness of Kadesh.
The voice of the Lord makes the deer give birth and lays bare the forests; and in his temple everyone speaks of his glory.
The Lord will dwell over the flood, and the Lord sits as king forever.
The Lord will give strength to his people; the Lord will bless his people with peace.
A Psalm of David.
I will exalt you, Lord, because you have lifted me up and have not let my enemies rejoice over me.
Lord my God, I cried out to you, and you healed me.
Lord, you brought my soul up from Hades, and you saved me from those who go down into the pit.
Sing to the Lord, you his faithful ones; give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness.
For anger is in his wrath, and life is in his favor. Weeping will lodge in the evening, and joy will come in the morning.
But I said in my prosperity, “I will never be shaken.”
Lord, by your favor give strength to my beauty. But you turned your face away from me, and I was troubled.
To you, Lord, I will cry out, and to my God I will pray.
What benefit is there in my blood when I go down into decay? Will the dust give thanks to you, or proclaim your righteousness?
The Lord heard and had mercy on me; the Lord became my helper.
You turned my mourning into joy for me; you tore off my sackcloth and clothed me with gladness.
So that my glory may sing to you, and I may not be pierced with sorrow. Lord my God, I will give thanks to you forever.
Glory. For the end. A Psalm of David.
In you, Lord, I have put my trust; let me be put to shame [?]. In your righteousness deliver me and rescue me.
Incline your ear to me (your ear); hurry to rescue me. Be my protecting God and a house of refuge to save me.
For you are my strength and my refuge; for your name’s sake you will guide me and nourish me.
You will bring me out of this net which they have hidden for me, for you are my protector, Lord.
Into your hands I will entrust my spirit; you have redeemed me, Lord, God of truth.
You have hated those who cling to empty vanities, but I have put my trust in the Lord.
I will rejoice and be glad in your mercy, because you have looked upon my lowliness; you have saved my soul from troubles.
And you have not shut me up in the hands of enemies; you have set my feet in a spacious place.
Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am in distress [?]. My eye is troubled by anger, and so are my soul and my inward parts.
For my life has wasted away in pain, and my years in sighing. My strength has failed through poverty, and my bones are troubled.
More than my enemies, I became an object of reproach, especially to my neighbors, and a terror to my acquaintances. Those who saw me outside fled from me.
I have been forgotten like a dead man, out of mind; I have become like a ruined vessel.
For I heard the slander of many who live around me. When they gathered together against me, they plotted to take my life.
But I put my hope in you, Lord; I said, “You are my God.”
My lot is in your hands. Deliver me from the hand of enemies, from those who persecute me.
Make your face shine upon your servant; save me by your mercy.
Lord, let me not be put to shame, for I have put my hope in you. Let the ungodly be put to shame and go down into Hades.
Let deceitful lips be silenced, those that speak lawlessness against the righteous with pride and contempt.
How abundant is your goodness, Lord, which you have stored up for those who fear you! You have shown it to those who put their hope in you, before the children of men.
You will hide them in the secrecy of your presence from human turmoil; you will shelter them in a shelter (a shelter) from the disputes of tongues.
Blessed is the Lord, for the Lord has made his mercy wondrous in a fortified city.
But I said in my terror, “I have been cast away from the sight of your eyes.” Therefore he heard the voice of my prayer when I cried out to you.
Love the Lord, all his faithful ones, for the Lord seeks truth, and the Lord repays those who act with excessive pride.
Be courageous, and let your hearts grow strong. All of you, put your hope in the Lord.
Of David. For understanding.
Blessed are those whose lawless deeds have been forgiven and whose sins have been covered.
Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not reckon sin, and in whose mouth there is no deceit.
For I kept silent, and my bones wasted away as I cried out all day long.
For day and night your hand weighed heavily upon me. I turned [?] to suffering when a thorn pierced me.
I acknowledged my lawlessness and did not cover up my sin. I said, “I will confess my lawlessness against myself to the Lord,” and you forgave the ungodliness of my heart.
Because of you, every faithful person will pray to you at a fitting time. Yet even in a flood of many waters, they will not come near him.
You are my refuge from the affliction that surrounds me. My joy, deliver me from those who wrong me.
I will give you understanding and guide you on the path you should take; I will fix my eyes on you.
Do not be like a horse or a mule, which have no understanding. You must restrain their jaws with bit and bridle when they will not come near you.
Many are the scourges of the sinner, but mercy will surround the one who trusts in the Lord.
Be glad in the Lord and rejoice, you righteous, and glory in him, all you who are upright in heart.
Glory. A Psalm of David. [?]
Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous; praise is fitting for the upright.
Give thanks to the Lord with harps; sing to him on a ten-stringed psaltery.
Sing him a new song; sing well to him with shouts of joy.
For the word of the Lord is right, and all his deeds are faithful.
The Lord loves mercy and justice; the earth is full of the Lord’s mercy.
By the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and all their host by the breath of his mouth.
He gathers the waters of the sea as into a wineskin; he places the depths in storehouses.
Let all the earth fear the Lord; let all who dwell in the world tremble before him.
For he spoke, and they came into being; he commanded, and they were created.
The Lord frustrates the counsel of nations; he rejects the plans of peoples and rejects the counsel of princes.
But the counsel of the Lord remains forever; the plans of his heart endure from generation to generation.
Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord, the people he has chosen as his own inheritance.
The Lord looked down from heaven; he saw all the children of humanity.
From his prepared dwelling he looked upon all who live on the earth.
He alone formed their hearts; he understands all their deeds.
A king is not saved by a great army; a mighty warrior is not saved by the greatness of his strength.
A horse is a false hope for salvation; it will not be saved by the greatness of your strength.
Look, the eyes of the Lord are upon those who fear him and upon those who hope in his mercy.
He will deliver their souls from death and sustain them in famine.
Our soul waits for the Lord, for he is our helper and protector.
For our hearts will rejoice in him, and we trust in his holy name.
May your mercy be upon us, Lord, just as we have hoped in you.
A psalm of David, when he changed his appearance before Abimelech, who dismissed him, and he went away.
I will bless the Lord at all times; his praise will always be in my mouth.
My soul will boast in the Lord; let the humble hear and rejoice.
Magnify the Lord with me, and let us exalt his name together.
I sought the Lord, and he heard me and delivered me from all my troubles.
Come to him and be enlightened, and your faces will not be put to shame.
This poor man cried out, and the Lord heard him and saved him from all his troubles.
The angel of the Lord will encamp around those who fear him and deliver them.
Taste and see that the Lord is good. Blessed is the man who trusts in him.
Fear the Lord, all his holy ones, for those who fear him lack nothing.
The rich have become poor and gone hungry, but those who seek the Lord will lack no good thing.
Come, children, listen to me; I will teach you the fear of the Lord.
Who is the person who desires life and loves to see good days?
Keep your tongue from evil and your lips from speaking deceit.
Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it.
The Lord's eyes are on the righteous, and his ears are attentive to their prayer.
But the Lord's face is against those who do evil, to wipe out their memory from the earth.
The righteous cried out, and the Lord heard them and delivered them from all their troubles.
The Lord is near to the brokenhearted, and he will save those who are humble in spirit.
The righteous have many troubles, but the Lord will deliver them from them all.
The Lord will preserve all their bones; not one of them will be broken.
The death of sinners is terrible, and those who hate the righteous will be guilty.
The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants, and none who trust in him will be guilty.
Glory. A psalm of David.
Judge, Lord, those who wrong me; fight against those who fight against me.
Take up weapons and a shield, and rise [?] to help me.
Draw your weapon and bar the way before those pursuing me. Say to my soul, “I am your salvation.”
Let those who seek my soul be ashamed and disgraced. Let those who plot evil against me turn back and be ashamed.
Let them be like dust before the wind, with the angel of the Lord [?] harassing them.
Let their way be dark and slippery, with the angel of the Lord pursuing them.
For without cause they hid their nets to destroy me; in vain they reviled my soul.
Let a net come upon him without his knowing; let the trap he hid catch him, and let him fall into another net.
My soul will rejoice in the Lord and delight in his salvation.
All my bones will say, “Lord, Lord, who is like you? You rescue the poor from the hands of those stronger than they are, and the poor and needy from those who plunder them.”
Unjust witnesses rose up against me; they questioned me about things I did not know.
They repaid me evil for good and left my soul bereft of children.
But when they acted vilely toward me, I clothed myself in sackcloth and humbled my soul with fasting, and my prayer returned to my own bosom.
As toward a neighbor, as toward our brother, so I sought to please him; as one weeping and mourning, so I humbled myself.
They rejoiced over me and gathered together. Blows gathered against me, and I did not know. They were divided and would not be still.
They tormented me and mocked me with mockery; they gnashed their teeth at me.
Lord, when will you look on? Restore my soul from their malice, my only life from the lions.
I will give thanks to you, Lord, in the great assembly; among a mighty people I will praise you.
Do not let those who are unjustly hostile to me rejoice over me, those who hate me without cause and wink their eyes.
For they spoke peacefully about me, yet devised deceit in anger.
They opened their mouths wide against me and said, “Good! Good! Our eyes have seen it!”
You have seen it, Lord; do not remain silent. Lord, do not withdraw from me.
Rise, Lord, attend to my judgment; my God and my Lord, attend to my cause.
Judge me, Lord, according to my righteousness, Lord my God, and do not let them rejoice over me.
Let them not say in their hearts, “Good, good! Just what we wanted!” Let them not say, “We have swallowed him up!”
Let those who rejoice at my misfortunes be ashamed and disgraced together. Let those who speak arrogantly against me be clothed in shame and disgrace.
Let those who desire my vindication rejoice and be glad. Let them always say, “May the Lord be exalted, who desires peace for his servant!”
And my tongue will meditate on your righteousness and your praise all day long.
For the end. Of David, the Lord’s servant.
The lawbreaker said that he would sin within himself, for there is no fear of God before his eyes.
For he acted deceitfully before him, to discover his own lawlessness and hate it.
The words of his mouth are lawlessness and deceit. He was unwilling to understand how to do good.
He plotted lawlessness on his bed. He took his stand on every path that was not good. Yet he was indignant at evil.
Lord, your mercy is in heaven, and your faithfulness reaches to the clouds.
Your righteousness is like the mountains of God; your judgments are a vast deep. You save humans and animals, Lord.
How greatly you have increased your mercy, O God! The children of humanity take refuge under the shelter of your wings.
They will drink their fill from the abundance of your house, and you will give them drink from the stream of your nourishment.
For with you is the fountain of life. In your light we will see light.
Extend your mercy to those who know you, and your righteousness to the upright in heart.
Let not the foot of pride come against me, and let not the sinner’s hand drive me away.
There all who practice lawlessness fell. They were cast down and cannot manage to stand.
Glory. A psalm of David.
Do not envy evildoers or be jealous of those who practice lawlessness.
For they will quickly wither like grass and soon fall away like green vegetation.
Trust in the Lord and do good. Dwell in the land, and you will feed on its riches.
Delight in the Lord, and he will grant you the requests of your heart.
Lay your way before the Lord and trust in him, and he will act.
He will bring forth your righteousness like the light, and your vindication like the noonday.
Submit to the Lord and plead with him. Do not envy (him) who prospers in your ways, the person who commits lawless acts.
Refrain from anger and abandon rage; do not let envy lead you to do evil.
For those who do evil will be destroyed, but those who wait for the Lord will possess the land.
In just a little while, the sinner will be no more; you will look for his place and will not find it.
But the meek will inherit the land and delight in abundant peace.
The sinner watches the righteous man and gnashes his teeth at him.
But the Lord will laugh at him, for he foresees that his day is coming.
The wicked have drawn their swords and bent their bow—a bitter deed [?]—to shoot the poor and needy and slaughter the upright in heart.
The sword [?] will enter their hearts, and their bows will not be broken.
A little belonging to a righteous man is better than the great wealth of sinners.
For the arms of sinners will be broken, but the Lord upholds the righteous man.
The Lord knows the path of the blameless, and their inheritance will last forever.
They will not be put to shame in an evil time, and in a day of famine they will have enough to eat.
For sinners will perish. But the Lord's enemies will be glorified together [?] and exalted [?]; fading away like smoke, they will vanish.
The sinner borrows and does not repay, but the righteous man shows mercy and gives.
For those who bless him will inherit the land, but those who curse him will be destroyed.
A person's steps are directed by the Lord, and he will greatly delight in his way.
When he falls, he will not be dashed to pieces, for the Lord holds up his hand.
I was young and have grown old, yet I have not seen a righteous man abandoned or his descendants begging for bread.
All day long the righteous man shows mercy and lends, and his descendants will be blessed.
Turn away from evil and do good, and live forever and ever.
For the Lord loves justice and will not abandon his faithful ones. They will be preserved forever; the lawless will be driven out, and the descendants of the ungodly will be destroyed.
But the righteous will inherit the land and dwell on it forever and ever.
The mouth of the righteous man meditates on wisdom, and his tongue speaks justice.
The law of his God is in his heart, and his steps will not falter.
The sinner watches the righteous man and seeks to kill him.
But the Lord will not leave him in his hands, nor condemn him when he is judged.
Wait for the Lord and keep his way, and he will exalt you to enjoy the land. When sinners are destroyed, you will see it.
I saw an ungodly man exalting himself and towering like the cedars of Lebanon.
I passed by, and behold, he was gone. I searched for him, but his place could not be found.
Preserve innocence and observe uprightness, for the peaceful man has a future.
But lawbreakers will be destroyed together; the descendants of the ungodly will be destroyed.
The salvation of the righteous comes from the Lord, and he is their defender in a time of trouble.
The Lord will help them and deliver them. He will rescue them from sinners and save them, because they trusted in him. Glory. Sitting.
A psalm of David. For remembrance.
Lord, do not rebuke me in your fury or punish me in your anger.
For your arrows have pierced me, and you have pressed your hand upon me.
There is no healing for my flesh because of your anger; there is no peace in my bones because of my sins.
For my lawless deeds have risen above my head; like a heavy burden, they weigh upon me.
My wounds have become foul and rotten because of my foolishness.
I have suffered and have been utterly bowed down; all day long I went about mourning.
For my loins are filled with mockery, and there is no healing for my flesh.
I was afflicted and greatly humbled; I roared because of the groaning of my heart.
Lord, all my longing is before you, and my groaning is not hidden from you.
My heart was troubled, and my strength deserted me; even the light of my eyes is no longer with me.
My friends and companions drew near, facing me, while my relatives stood far away.
Those seeking my life pressed hard. Those seeking to harm me spoke empty words, and I pondered deceitful things all day.
But like a deaf man, I did not hear, and like a mute man, I did not open my mouth.
I became like a man who does not hear and has no rebukes in his mouth.
For I trusted in you, Lord, and you heard me, Lord my God.
For I said, “Let my enemies never rejoice over me.” When my feet slipped, they boasted against me.
For I am ready for wounds, and my pain is always before me.
For I will declare my lawlessness, and I will be concerned about my sin.
But my living enemies have grown stronger than I, and those who hate me unjustly have multiplied.
Those who repay me evil for good slandered me because I pursued goodness.
Do not abandon me, O Lord my God; do not withdraw from me.
Attend to my help, O Lord of my salvation.
For the end. A song of David.
I said, “I will guard my ways so that I do not sin with my tongue.” I placed a guard over my mouth when the sinner rose against me.
I became mute and humbled myself, and kept silent even about good things; and my pain was renewed.
My heart grew hot [?] within me, and as I meditated, a fire blazed up. I spoke with my tongue:
“Tell me, O Lord, my end, and what the [?] of my days is, so that I may understand what I lack.”
See, you have made my days a handbreadth in length, and my existence is as nothing before you. Indeed, every living [?] person is altogether vanity. Interlude.
Indeed, a person walks about as an image; yet he is troubled in vain. He stores things up and does not know for whom he will gather them.
And now, who is my patient hope? Is it not the Lord? And my existence rests with you.
Deliver me from all my lawless deeds. You have made me an object of reproach to the fool.
I became mute [?] and did not open [?] my mouth, because you did it.
Take your blows away from me, for I have wasted away under the strength of your hand.
In rebuking lawlessness, you have shown man; you have made his soul waste away like a spider’s web. Indeed, every person is in vain.
Hear my prayer, O Lord, and give ear to my plea. Do not be silent at my tears, for I am a sojourner with you and a stranger, as all my fathers were.
Give me relief so that I may rest, before I depart and am no more.
For the end. A psalm of David.
I waited patiently for the Lord, and he attended to me and heard my prayer.
He brought me up from the pit of suffering and from the muddy mire. He set my feet upon a rock and made my steps firm.
He put a new song into my mouth, a song to our God. Many will see [?] and be afraid, and they will trust in the Lord.
Blessed is the man whose hope is the name of the Lord, who has not looked to vain things and false madness.
You have done many wonderful things, Lord my God, and no one can compare with you in your thoughts. I proclaimed and spoke of them; they are more than can be counted.
You did not desire sacrifice and offering, but you prepared a body for me. You did not ask for burnt offerings for sin.
Then I said, “See, I am coming. In the scroll of the book it is written about me.”
I desired to do your will, my God, and your law is within my heart.
I proclaimed the good news of your righteousness in the great assembly. See, I have not restrained my lips; Lord, you know.
I have not hidden your righteousness within my heart. I have spoken of your faithfulness and your salvation. I have not [?] your mercy and your truth [?] from the great assembly.
But you, Lord, do not keep your compassion far from me. Your mercy and your truth have always protected me.
For evils beyond counting have surrounded me. My lawless deeds have overtaken me, and I could not see. They have become more numerous than the hairs of my head, and my heart has failed me.
Be pleased, Lord, to deliver me. Lord, look to my help.
Let those who seek to take my life be ashamed and disgraced together. Let those who wish me harm turn back [?] and be ashamed.
Let those who say to me, “Aha, aha!” receive their shame at once.
Let all who seek you [?], Lord, rejoice and be glad in you. Let those who love your [?] always say, “May the Lord be exalted [?]!”
But I am poor and needy; the Lord will care for me. You are my helper [?] and my protector [?]. My God, do not delay [?].
GLORY. FOR THE END. A PSALM OF DAVID.
Blessed is the one who considers the poor and needy. On a day of trouble [?], the Lord will deliver [?].
The Lord will protect [?] him and keep him alive, and make him blessed [?] on the earth. He will not hand him over [?] into the hands of his enemies [?].
The Lord will help him on his sickbed [?]. You have turned over [?] his whole bed [?] in his illness.
I [?] said, “Lord, have mercy on me. Heal my soul [?], for I have sinned against you [?].”
My enemies [?] spoke evil against me: “When will he die [?] and his name perish [?]?”
He would come in to look and speak empty words. His heart gathered lawlessness for itself. He would go outside and speak.
All my enemies whispered together against me [?]. They plotted [?] evil against me.
They laid a lawless accusation [?] against me [?]: “Will the one who sleeps [?] not rise again [?]?”
For even the man who was at peace with me [?], in whom I trusted, who ate my bread [?], has greatly increased [?] his treachery against me.
But you, Lord, have mercy [?] on me and raise me up, and I will repay them [?].
By this I have known that you were pleased with me: my enemy will not rejoice [?] over me.
But you received me in my innocence [?]; you established me before you forever.
Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, from age to age. So be it, so be it.
For the end. For understanding. For the sons of Korah. A psalm of David.
As a deer longs for springs of water, so my soul longs for you, O God.
My soul has thirsted for the mighty and living God. When shall I come and appear before the face of God?
My tears have been my bread day and night, while they said to me every day, “Where is your God?”

I remembered these things and poured out my soul within me. For I will pass through the place of the wondrous tabernacle to the house of God, amid voices of joy and thanksgiving, the sound of one celebrating.
Why are you sorrowful, my soul, and why do you trouble me? Hope in God, for I will praise him, the salvation of my countenance and my God.
My soul was troubled within me. Therefore I remembered you from the land of the Jordan and Hermon, from the little mountain.
Deep calls to deep at the sound of its waterfalls. All your surges and your waves will pass over me (over me).
By day the Lord will command his mercy, and at night his song comes from me, a prayer to the God of my life.
I will say to my God, “You are my defender. Why have you forgotten me? And why do I go about mourning because of the oppression of my enemy?”
When my bones were being crushed, my enemies taunted me, saying to me every day, “Where is your God?”
Why are you sorrowful, my soul, and why do you trouble me? Hope in God, for I will praise him, the salvation of my countenance and my God.
A psalm of David.
Vindicate me, O God, and defend my cause against an ungodly nation. Deliver me from the unjust and deceitful man.
For you, O God, are my strength. Why have you rejected me? And why do I go about mourning when the enemy oppresses me?
Send out your light and your truth. They have guided me and brought me to your holy mountain and to your dwelling places.
And I will go to the altar of God, to God who makes my youth rejoice. I will praise you with the harp, O my God.
Why are you downcast, my soul, and why do you trouble me? Hope in God, for I will praise him, the salvation of my countenance and my God.
Glory. For the end. For understanding. For the sons of Korah. A psalm.
O God, we have heard with our own ears; our fathers have told us the deeds you did in their days, in the former days of old.
Your hand uprooted nations, and you planted them; you afflicted peoples and drove them in.
For they did not inherit [?] the land by their own weapons, nor did their own arm save them, but your right hand and your arm and the light of your face, because you were pleased with them.
You yourself are my King and my God, who commands deliverance for Jacob.
Through you we will gore our enemies with our horns, and through your name we will bring to nothing those who rise against us.
For I do not trust in my bow, and my weapon will not save me.
You have saved us from those who oppress us, and you have put those who hate us to shame.
In God we will boast all day long, and we will praise your name forever. Selah.
But now you have rejected us and put us to shame, and you do not go out with our armies, O God.
You have made us turn back before our enemies, and those who hate us have plundered us for themselves.
You have given us up like sheep for food, and you have scattered us among the nations.
You sold your people for no price, and our shouts were not many.
You have made us a reproach to our neighbors, an object of mockery and ridicule to those around us.
You have made us a byword among the nations, a covering of the head among the peoples.
My disgrace is before me all day long, and the shame of my face has covered me,
because of the voice of the one who insults and slanders, because of the presence of the pursuing enemy.
All these things have come upon us, yet we have not forgotten you or broken your covenant.
Our heart has not turned back, and you have turned our path away from your way.
For you have humbled us in a place of affliction, and the shadow of death has covered us.
If we have forgotten the name of our God, or if we have stretched out our hands to a foreign god,
will God not search these things out? For he knows the secrets of the heart.
For your sake we are put to death all day long; we have been counted as sheep for slaughter.
Awake! Why do you sleep, Lord? Arise, and do not reject us forever.
Why do you turn your face away and forget our poverty and our affliction?
For our soul has been brought down to the dust; my belly clings to the ground.
Arise, Lord, help us; bring deliverance for the sake of your name.
For the end. Concerning those who are changed. For the sons of Korah. For understanding. A psalm. About the beloved David.
My heart has poured forth a good word. I speak (I [?]) of my works to the king. My tongue is the pen of a swift scribe.
You are more beautiful than the sons of men. Grace has been poured out upon your lips; therefore God will bless you forever.
Gird your sword on your thigh, mighty one, in your beauty and your splendor.
Draw your bow, prosper, and reign for the sake of truth, gentleness, and righteousness. And your right hand will guide [?].
Your arrows are sharpened, mighty one. Your peoples will fall beneath you; the arrows pierce the hearts of the king’s enemies.
Your throne, O God, is forever and ever; the scepter of your kingdom is a scepter of uprightness.
You have loved righteousness and hated lawlessness. Therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions.
Myrrh, stacte, and cassia come from your garments, from ivory halls, from which they have gladdened you.
Kings’ daughters are among those who honor you. The queen stood at your right hand, clothed and adorned in gold-embroidered garments.
Listen, daughter, and look; incline your ear. Forget your people and your father’s house.
And the king will desire your beauty, for he is your God.
Bow down to him. And the daughter of Tyre will come with gifts; the rich among the people will seek your favor.
All the glory of the king’s daughter is within; she is clothed and adorned with golden fringes.
Virgins will be brought to the king, and companions will be brought to you.
They will be brought with gladness and joy; they will be brought into the king’s temple.
Your sons have taken the place of your fathers. They appointed them princes throughout all the earth.
They will remember your name in every generation. Therefore the peoples will praise you forever and ever.
A Psalm of David. For the end. Concerning the sons of Korah. Concerning hidden things.
God is our refuge and strength, a helper in the severe troubles that have come upon us.
Therefore we will not be afraid when the earth is shaken and the mountains are moved into the depths of the seas.
Their waters roared and were troubled; the mountains were shaken by his might.
The river’s streams gladden the city of God. The Most High has made his dwelling holy.
God is in its midst, and it will not be shaken. God will help it at the break of dawn.
The nations were thrown into turmoil, and the kingdoms were subdued. The Most High uttered his voice, and the earth shook.
The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our defender.
Come and see the works of God, who has worked wonders on the earth.
He brings wars to an end throughout the earth. He will crush the bow, break the weapons, and burn the shields with fire.
Be still and know that I am God. I will be exalted among the nations; I will be exalted on the earth.
The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our defender.
Glory. Sessional hymn. A psalm concerning the sons of Korah.
All you nations, clap your hands; shout to God with a voice of joy.
For God is most high and awe-inspiring, a great king over all the earth.
He subjected peoples to us and nations beneath our feet.
He chose us as his inheritance, the beauty of Jacob, which he loved.
God has gone up with shouting, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet.
Sing to our God, sing; sing to our king, sing.
For God is king of all the earth; sing with understanding.
God reigns over all the nations; God sits on his holy throne.
The rulers of the peoples gathered with the God of Abraham. For the mighty of the earth belong to God; he has been greatly exalted.
A song for the sons of Korah, on the Sabbath.
Our Lord is great and greatly praised in the city of our God and on his holy mountain,
firmly rooted, the joy of all the earth: the slopes of Mount Zion on the north, the city of the great king.
God is known in its fortresses when he defends it.
For the kings of the earth gathered; they came together.
They saw it and were astonished; [?]; they were shaken.
Trembling seized them there, pain like that of a woman in labor [?].
With a stormy wind you shattered the ships of Tarshish.
As we have heard, so we have seen in the city of the God of hosts, in the city of our God. God established it forever.
We have received your mercy, O God, in the midst of your people.
As your name, O God, so your praise reaches to the ends of the earth. Your right hand is full of your righteousness.
Let Mount Zion rejoice; let the daughters of Judah be glad because of your judgments, O Lord.
Walk around Zion and encircle it; count its towers.
Set your hearts on his strength, and divide up his house, so that he may tell it to another generation.
For he is our God forever and ever; he will shepherd us forever.
For the end. For the sons of Korah.
Hear this, all nations; listen to this, all who live throughout the world.
Both the earthborn and the sons of men, rich and poor together.
My mouth will speak wisdom, and the meditation of my heart will be understanding.
I will incline my ear to a parable; I will unfold my riddle on the harp.
Why am I afraid on an evil day? The lawlessness of my way has surrounded me.
Those who trust in their own strength and boast of the abundance of their wealth.
A brother will not redeem; will a man redeem? He will not give God a ransom for himself,
or the price of the redemption of his soul.
And he established himself forever and will live to the end. He will not see destruction when he sees the wise dying.
The fool and the senseless person will perish together and leave their wealth to strangers.
And their graves and their houses are forever, and their settlements from generation to generation. They gave their own names to lands.
And man, though held in honor, did not understand. He was ranked with senseless beasts and became like them.
This way of theirs is a stumbling block to them, and afterward they will take pleasure in their own words.

Like sheep they have been placed in Hades; death will shepherd them. The upright will rule over them in the morning, and their help (and their help) will waste away in Hades. They were cast out from their glory.
But God will redeem my soul from the hand of Hades when he receives me.
Let him not be afraid when a man becomes rich, or when the glory of his house increases.
When he dies [?], will he not leave everything behind? Nor will the glory of his house go down with him.
For his soul will be blessed during his life. He will give thanks to you when you do good to him.
He will enter the company of his fathers; he will see light forever.
Man, though held in honor, did not understand. He was ranked with senseless beasts and became like them. Glory.
A psalm of Asaph.
The God of gods, the Lord, has spoken ([?]) and called the earth, from the rising of the sun to its setting.
From Zion comes the beauty of his splendor; God will come openly.
Our God will not remain silent. Fire will blaze before him, and a mighty storm will surround him.
He will summon heaven from above, and the earth, to judge his people.
He will gather his holy ones, those who make his covenant through sacrifices.
And the heavens will proclaim his righteousness, for God is judge. Interlude.
Hear, my people, and I will speak to you; Israel, I will testify to you, for I am God, your God.
I will not rebuke you for your sacrifices; your burnt offerings are always before me.
I will not accept a bull from your house, or goats from your flocks.
For all the wild animals of the woods are mine, as are the livestock on the mountains and the oxen.
I know all the birds of heaven, and mighty beauty is with me.
If I grow hungry, I will not tell you, for the world and everything in it are mine.
Do I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?
Offer God a sacrifice of praise, and fulfill your vows to the Most High.
And call upon me on the day of my distress; I will deliver you, and you will glorify me.
But God said to the sinner: Why do you recite my statutes and take my covenant upon your lips?
Yet you hated my discipline and cast my words behind you.
When you saw a thief, you ran with him, and you joined company with an adulterer.
Your mouth multiplied evil, and your tongue wove deceit.
You sat and slandered your brother, and laid a stumbling block for your mother's son.
You did these things, and I remained silent. I imagined lawlessness [?], that I would be like you. I will rebuke you and set your sins before your face.
Understand this, all you nations who forget God, lest he seize you and there be no one to deliver you.
A sacrifice of praise will glorify me, and I will go along the path by which I will reveal my salvation.
For the end. A psalm of David.
When Dathan the prophet came to him, after he had gone in to Bathsheba.
Have mercy on me, O God, according to your great mercy, and according to your abundant compassion cleanse me of my lawless deeds.
Wash me thoroughly from my lawlessness, and cleanse me from my sin.
For I know my lawlessness, and my sin is always before me.
Against you alone I have sinned, and I have done evil before you, so that you may be justified in your words and prevail when you are judged.
For behold, I was conceived in lawlessness, and in sins my mother bore me.
For behold, you have loved truth; you have revealed to me the hidden and secret things of your wisdom.
You will sprinkle me with hyssop, and I will be cleansed; you will wash me, and I will become whiter than snow.
You will let me hear joy and gladness; the bones that have been humbled will rejoice.
Turn your face away from my sins, and blot out all my lawlessness.
Create a clean heart in me, O God, and renew an upright spirit within me.
Do not cast me away from your presence, and do not take your Holy Spirit from me.
Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and strengthen me with a ruling spirit.
I will teach the lawless your ways, and the ungodly will return to you.
Deliver me from bloodguilt, O God, God of my salvation; my tongue will rejoice in your righteousness.
Lord, you will open my lips, and my mouth will proclaim your praise.
For if you had desired a sacrifice, I would have given it; you take no pleasure in burnt offerings.
A sacrifice to God is a broken spirit; God will not despise a broken and humbled heart.
Do good to Zion in your favor, Lord, and let the walls of Jerusalem be built.
Then you will take pleasure in a sacrifice of righteousness, in offerings and burnt offerings; then they will place young bulls on your altar.
Glory. For the end. For understanding. Of David, when Doeg the Edomite came and reported to Saul
and said to him, “Abimelech came into David’s house.”
Why do you boast of evil, mighty man? Lawlessness all day long.
Your tongue has devised injustice; like a sharpened razor, you have worked deceit.
You have loved evil more than goodness, injustice rather than speaking what is right.
You have loved every destructive word, deceitful tongue.
Therefore God will destroy you completely; he will tear you out and remove you from your dwelling, and uproot you from the land of the living.
The righteous will see and be afraid; they will laugh at him and say:
“Here is the man who did not make God his helper, but trusted in the abundance of his wealth and grew strong through his vanity.”
But I am like a fruitful olive tree in the house of God. I have trusted in God’s mercy forever and ever.
I will give thanks to you forever, because you have done this. I will wait for your name, for you are good in the presence of your holy ones.
For the end. Concerning Mahalath. For understanding. Of David.
The fool said in his heart, “There is no God.” They became corrupt and loathsome in their lawless deeds. There is no one who does good.
The Lord looked down from heaven upon humankind to see whether anyone understood or sought God.
They have all turned aside; together they have become worthless. There is no one who does good, not even one.
Do all those who practice lawlessness not understand? They devour my people as though eating bread, and they have not called upon God.
There they were terrified where there was nothing to fear, because God scattered the bones of those who seek to please people. They were put to shame because God despised them.
Who will bring Israel’s salvation from Zion? When God restores his people from captivity, Jacob will rejoice and Israel will be glad.
For the end. Concerning their songs. For understanding. Of David.
When the Ziphites came and said to Saul, “Is not David [?] among us?”
O God, save me by your name, and judge my case by your power.
O God, hear my prayer; listen to the words of my mouth.
For strangers have risen against me, and powerful men have sought my life. They have not set God before them.
Look, God helps me, and the Lord is the defender of my life.
Return evil upon my enemies; in your truth I will destroy them.
I will sacrifice to you willingly. I will give thanks to your name, O Lord, for it is good.
For you have delivered me from every affliction, and my eye has looked upon my enemies.
For the end. Among them. For understanding. A psalm of David.
Listen to my prayer, O God, and do not disregard my plea.
Pay attention to me and hear me. I grieved in my sorrow and was troubled
by the enemy’s voice and the sinner’s oppression, because they brought lawlessness upon me and were hostile to me in their anger.
My heart was troubled within me, and the fear of death fell upon me.
Pain and trembling came upon me, and darkness covered me.
And I said, “Who will give me wings like a dove, so that I may fly away and rest?”
Look, I fled far away. Pause. And I settled in the wilderness.
I waited for God, who saves me from faintness of spirit and from the storm.
Drown them, Lord, and divide their tongues, for I have seen lawlessness and strife in the city.
Day and night they go around it upon its walls, and lawlessness, trouble, and injustice are within it.
Usury and deceit have never left its streets.
For if an enemy had insulted me, I would have endured it; and if someone who hated me had spoken arrogantly against me, I would have hidden from him.
But it was you, a man of one mind with me, my leader and my acquaintance,
you who made food sweet for me when we ate together. We walked together in God's temple, united in mind.
Let death come upon them, and let them go down alive into Hades, for wickedness is in their dwelling and among them.
I cried out to God, and the Lord heard me.
Evening, morning, and noon I will speak and declare my trouble, and he will hear my voice.
He will deliver my soul in peace from those who draw near me, for there were many with me.
God will hear and humble them, he who exists from before the ages. Pause. For there is no change in them, and they have not feared God.
He will stretch out his hand to repay them; they have profaned his covenant.
They were scattered by the anger of your face, and their hearts drew near. Their words became softer than oil, yet they are arrows.
Cast your care upon God, and he will sustain you. He will never allow the righteous to be shaken.
But you, God, will bring them down into the pit of destruction. A man of bloodshed and deceit will not live out half his days. But I, Lord, have trusted in you. Glory. Kathisma 7.
For the end. Concerning the people far removed from the holy ones. An inscription of David, when the foreigners seized him in Egypt.
Have mercy on me, God, for a man has trampled me; all day long he has oppressed me with his attacks.
My enemies have trampled me all day long, those who fight against me from on high.
By day I will not be afraid; but I have trusted [?] you.
In God I will praise my words; in God I trust, and I will not fear what flesh can do to me.
