All day long my words were hateful to them; all their thoughts against me were for evil.
They gather and hide themselves; they watch my heel, just as they have waited for my life.
You will by no means save them; in your anger you will bring down the peoples, O God.
I have declared my life to you. You have set [?] my tears before you, according to your promise.
My enemies will turn back on whatever day we call upon you. By this I have known that you are my God.
In God I will praise the utterance; in the Lord I will praise the word.
I trust in God and will not fear what a human being can do to me.
God’s vows are within me, which I will fulfill in praise of you.
For he has delivered my soul from death, my eyes from tears, and my feet from stumbling. I will be pleasing before the Lord in the light of the living.
For the end. Do not destroy. Of David, for an inscription on a pillar, when he fled from Saul into the cave.
Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me, for my soul trusts in you. In the shadow of your wings I will place my hope until lawlessness passes away.
I will cry out to God Most High, to God who has done good to me.
He sent from heaven and saved me. He will bring those who trample me into disgrace. God sent his mercy and his truth.
He has delivered my soul from among young lions. I lay down to sleep in distress. The sons of men—their teeth are weapons and arrows, and their tongue is a sharp sword.
Be exalted above the heavens, O God, and let your glory be over all the earth.
They prepared a net for my feet and bowed down my soul. They dug a pit before me and fell into it themselves.
My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready. I sing and will sing praise to my glory.
Awake, my glory! Awake, harp and lyre! I will arise early.
I will give thanks to you among the peoples, O Lord; I will sing praise to you among the nations.
For your mercy has reached the heavens, and your truth the clouds.
Be exalted above the heavens, O God, and let your glory be over all the earth.
For the end. Do not destroy. Of David, for an inscription on a pillar. A psalm of David.
If you truly speak righteousness, judge uprightly, you sons of men.
For in your hearts you practice lawlessness on earth; your hands weave injustice.
Sinners have been estranged from the womb; they have gone astray from birth, speaking lies.
Their fury is like that of a serpent, like a deaf asp that stops its ears.
Which will not hear the voice of the charmer, though charmed by a skilled enchanter.
God will shatter their teeth in their mouths; the Lord has shattered the lions’ molars.
They will vanish like water flowing past; they will draw their bow until they grow weak.
Like melted wax they will be swept away. Fire fell upon them, and they did not see the sun.
Before you recognize the thorns of your buckthorn, he will swallow you up alive, as in wrath.
The righteous man will rejoice when he sees vengeance; he will wash his hands in the sinner’s blood.
And a person will say, “There is indeed fruit for the righteous man; there is indeed a God who judges them on earth.” Glory.
For the end. Do not destroy. Of David. For an inscription. When Saul sent men to watch his house, to kill him.
Rescue me from my enemies, my God, and deliver me from those who rise against me.
Deliver me from those who practice lawlessness, and save me from the bloodthirsty and deceitful man.
For see, they have hunted down my soul; mighty men have attacked me. It is not because of my lawlessness or my sin, Lord.
Without wrongdoing I ran and kept a straight course. Rise to meet me and see.
And you, Lord God of hosts, God of Jacob, take heed and visit all the nations. Have no mercy on any who practice lawlessness.
They will return at evening and grow hungry like dogs, and go around the city.
See, they speak out with their mouths, and weapons are in their mouths, for they say, “Who hears?”
But you, Lord, will laugh at them; you will bring the nations to nothing.
I will keep my strength for you, for you, God, are my protector.
My God—his mercy will go before me. My God will let me look upon my enemies.
Do not kill them, lest they forget your law. Scatter them by your power and bring them down, Lord, my defender.
The sin of their mouths is the word of their lips, and they will be caught in your pride. And because of their cursing and lying they will be exposed at the end.
In the wrath of destruction they will be no more. And they will know that God rules over Jacob, to the ends of the earth.
They will return at evening and grow hungry like dogs, and go around the city.
They will scatter in search of food, and if they are not satisfied, they will grumble.
But I will sing of your strength, and in the morning I will rejoice in your mercy. For you have been my protector and my refuge in the day of my distress.
You are my helper; I will sing to you. For you, God, are my protector, my God, my mercy.
For the end. For those who will be changed. A pillar inscription of David. For instruction.
When he burned Syrian Mesopotamia and the Syria of Zobah, and Joab returned and struck [?] in the Valley of Salt.
O God, you have rejected us and broken us down. You have been angry and have shown us mercy.
You shook the earth and troubled it. Heal its fractures, for it is trembling.
You have shown your people harsh things; you have given us wine of remorse to drink.
You have given those who fear you a sign, so that they may flee from the bow.
So that all your beloved may be delivered, save by your right hand and hear me.
God has spoken in his sanctuary: “I will rejoice and divide Shechem, and measure out the valley of settlements.
Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine. Ephraim is the strength of my head; Judah is my king.
Moab is the cooking pot of my hope. Over Edom I will stretch out my sandal. Foreign peoples have submitted to me.”
Who will lead me into the besieged city? Who will guide me as far as Edom?
Will it not be you, O God, who rejected us? And will you not go out, O God, with our armies?
Give us help in distress, for human deliverance is futile.
With God we will act mightily, and he will bring to nothing those who afflict us.
For the end. With songs. Of David.
Hear my prayer, O God; attend to my supplication.
From the ends of the earth I cried out to you. When my heart grew faint, you raised me onto a rock [?].
You have guided me, for you have become my hope, a tower of strength against the enemy.
I will dwell in your tent forever; I will take shelter beneath the covering of your wings.
For you, O God, have heard my prayer. You have given an inheritance to those who fear your name.
Add days to the king’s days; may his years extend through generation after generation.
He will remain forever before God. Who will seek out his mercy and truth?
Thus I will sing to your name forever, fulfilling my vows day by day.
Glory. A psalm of David.
Will not my soul submit to God? For my salvation comes from him.
For he is my God, my Savior, my protector; I will not be greatly shaken.
How long will you attack a man and kill him, all of you, as though he were a leaning wall or a fence pushed over?
Yet they plotted to cast down my honor; they ran in thirst [?]. With their mouths they blessed, but in their hearts they cursed.
Yet my soul will submit to God, for my salvation comes from him.
For he is my God, my Savior, my protector; I will not be moved.
My salvation and my glory rest with God. God is my help, and my hope is in God.
Trust in him, all you gathered people; pour out your hearts before him, for God is our helper.
Yet the sons of men are empty; [?] the sons of men are deceitful, failing to measure up on the scales. [?] Together they are emptiness.
Do not trust in injustice, and do not desire plunder. If wealth flows your way, do not set your heart on it.
God has spoken once; I have heard these two things: that power belongs to God,
and mercy belongs to you, Lord, for you will repay each person according to their deeds.
A psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Edom.
O God, my God, I seek you at dawn. My soul thirsts for you. How often my flesh longs for you in a deserted, impassable, waterless land!
Thus I appeared before you in the sanctuary, to see your power and your glory.
For your mercy is better than my life; my lips will praise you.
So I will bless you throughout my life; in your name I will lift up my hands.
My soul will be filled as with rich food and fat, and my mouth will praise you with joyful lips.
When I remembered you on my bed, I meditated on you in the early morning hours.
For you have been my helper, and in the shelter of your wings I will rejoice.
My soul clings to you, and your right hand has upheld me.
But they sought my life in vain. Let them go down into the depths of the earth.
They will be handed over to the sword; they will become portions for foxes.
But the king will rejoice in God, and everyone who swears by him will boast, for the mouths of those who speak injustice have been stopped.
For the end. A psalm of David.
Hear my voice, O God, when I pray to you. Deliver my soul from fear of the enemy.
Hide me from the gathering of the wicked, from the multitude of those who do wrong.
They sharpened their tongues like weapons and bent their bow—a bitter word—
to shoot secretly at the blameless. Suddenly they will shoot at him and will not be afraid.
They strengthened themselves in an evil plan. They spoke of hiding snares and said, “Who will see them?”
They searched out lawlessness; those searching out lawlessness have vanished. A man will draw near, and the heart is deep,
and God will be exalted. Their wounds became like children’s arrows.
Their tongues grew powerless among them. All who saw them were troubled.
And everyone was afraid. They proclaimed the works of God and understood what he had done.
The righteous will rejoice in the Lord and trust in him, and all the upright in heart will glory.
Glory. Sessional hymn. For the end. A psalm of David. A song of Jeremiah and Ezekiel and the people, concerning their return, when they were about to depart.
A song is fitting for you, O God, in Zion, and a vow will be fulfilled to you in Jerusalem.
Hear my prayer, O God, and all flesh will come to you.
The words of the lawless have overpowered us, but you will cleanse our ungodliness.
Blessed is the one whom you chose and received; he will dwell in your courts. We have been filled with the good things of your house. Your temple is holy, wonderful in righteousness.
Hear us, O God our Savior, the hope of all the ends of the earth and of those far away at sea.
You establish the mountains by your strength, girded with power.
You stir up the depths of the sea; who can withstand the roar of its waves? The nations will be shaken,
and those living at the ends of the earth will be afraid of your signs. You will adorn the coming of morning and evening.
You visited the earth and watered it; you greatly enriched it. The river of God was filled with water. You prepared food for them, for such is your preparation.
Water its furrows and multiply its grain; in its showers, what sprouts will rejoice.
You will bless the crown of the year with your goodness, and your fields will be filled with abundance.
The beautiful places of the wilderness will grow rich, and the hills will gird themselves with joy.
The rams of the flock have clothed themselves, and the valleys will abound in wheat. They will cry out and sing.
For the end. A psalm of David. For adornment [?].
Shout to God, all the earth!
Sing to his name; give glory to his praise.
Say to God, “How fearsome are your works! Because of the greatness of your power, your enemies will lie to you.”
Let all the earth worship you and sing to you; let them sing to your name, O Most High. Pause.
Come and see the works of God: how fearsome he is in his purposes beyond the sons of men!
He turns the sea into dry land; they will cross the river on foot. There let us rejoice in him,
who rules with your glory forever [?]. His eyes watch the nations. Let those who are angry not exalt themselves.
Bless our God, you nations, and make the sound of his praise heard.
He has kept my soul alive and has not let my feet stumble.
For you have tested us, O God; you have refined us as silver is refined.
You brought us into a net; you laid affliction upon our backs.
You set a man over our heads. We passed through fire and water, and you brought us out into comfort.
I will enter your house with burnt offerings; I will fulfill my vows to you,
which my lips uttered and my mouth spoke in my distress.
I will offer you burnt offerings of fattened animals, with incense. I will offer you rams, bulls, and goats.
Come, listen, and I will tell you, all who fear God, everything he has done for my soul.
I cried out to him with my mouth, and exalted him beneath my tongue.
If I have regarded wrongdoing in my heart, do not hear me, O God.
For this reason God heard me; he attended to the sound of my prayer.
Blessed is God, who will not reject my prayer or withhold his mercy from me.
For the end. A psalm. A song [?]. With singing.
O God, have mercy on us and bless us; make your face shine upon us and have mercy on us,
so that we may know your way on earth, your salvation among all nations.
Let the peoples praise you, O God; let all the peoples praise you.
Let the nations rejoice and be glad, for you judge the peoples justly and guide the nations on earth.
Let the peoples praise you, O God; let all the peoples praise you.
The earth will yield its fruit. Bless us, O God,
our God. And let all the ends of the earth fear him. GLORY.
For the end. A psalm of David.
Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered; let those who hate him flee from his presence.
As smoke vanishes, let them vanish. As wax melts before fire, so let sinners perish before God.
But let the righteous be glad and rejoice before God; let them delight in gladness.
Sing to God; sing praises to his name. Make a way for him who rides upon the west. The Lord is his name; rejoice before him. They will be troubled at his presence.
The father of orphans and the judge of widows is God in his holy place.
God settles those of one mind in a house. He brings out those in chains with might, and likewise those who provoke him and those who live in tombs.
O God, when you went out before your people, when you passed through the wilderness,
the earth shook, and the heavens dripped before the God of Zion, before the God of Israel [?].
You will set apart a willing rain, O God, for your inheritance. It grew weak, but you restored it.
Your creatures dwell in it. In your goodness you provided for the poor, O God.
The Lord will give a word to the one proclaiming good news with great power.
The king of the hosts of the beloved; for the beauty of the house to divide the spoil.
If you sleep between the boundaries, the wings of a dove are covered with silver, and its back gleams with gold.
When the heavenly one scatters kings upon it, they will be snow-covered [?] in Zalmon.
The mountain of God is a rich mountain, a rugged mountain, a rich mountain.
Why do you suppose, you rugged mountains? This is the mountain in which God was pleased to dwell; indeed, the Lord will dwell there forever.
The chariot of God is tens of thousands upon tens of thousands, thousands of those who flourish. The Lord is among them in holy Zion.
You have ascended on high; you have taken captives; you have received a gift among humankind, so that even those who resist may dwell there. The Lord God is blessed.
Blessed is the Lord. Day by day the God of our salvation will help us.
Our God is a God who saves, and to the Lord, the Lord, belong the ways out of death.
But God will crush the heads of his enemies, the hairy crown of those who persist in their transgressions.
The Lord said, “I will bring back from Bashan; I will bring back in the depths of the sea.”
Let your foot be washed in blood, and the tongue of your [?] in that of your enemies, from him.
Your processions were seen, O God, the processions of my God, the King who is in the sanctuary.
The princes went ahead, [?] the singers, among the women playing tambourines.
Bless God in the assemblies, the Lord, you who come from the springs of Israel.
There is Benjamin, the young man, in an astonished state of mind; the princes of Judah, their rulers; the princes of Zebulun and Naphtali.
Give your command, O God, by your power. Make firm, O God, what you have accomplished among us.
From your temple in Jerusalem, they will bring gifts to you, O King.
Rebuke the beasts of the reeds, the herd of bulls among the peoples’ heifers, to shut in those tested with silver. Scatter the nations that desire war.
Supplicants will come from Egypt, and Ethiopia will hasten to stretch out her hands to God.
Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; sing praises to the Lord,
who ascended into the heaven of heavens in the east. See, he will give his voice a voice of power.
Give glory to God. His majesty is over Israel, and his power is in the clouds.
God is wonderful among his holy ones, the God of Israel. He will give strength and might to his people. Blessed be God.
GLORY.
Save me, O God, for the waters have reached my soul.
I sank into deep mire, and there is no firm footing. I came into the depths of the sea, and a storm overwhelmed me.
I grew weary from crying out, and my throat fell silent. My eyes failed as I waited for my God.
Those who hate me without cause have become more numerous than the hairs of my head. My enemies, who persecute me unjustly, have grown strong. Then I repaid what I had not stolen.
O God, you know my lawlessness, and my transgressions have not been hidden from you.
Do not let those who wait for you be put to shame because of me, O Lord, Lord of hosts. Do not let those who seek you be disgraced because of me, O God of Israel.
For your sake I have borne reproach; shame has covered my face.
I became a stranger to my brothers and a foreigner to my mother’s sons.
For zeal for your house has consumed me, and the reproaches of those who reproach you have fallen upon me.
I covered my soul with fasting, and it became a reproach to me.
I made sackcloth my clothing, and I became a byword to them.
Those who sat at the gates mocked me, and those who drank wine sang about me.
But my prayer is to you, Lord, at the time of your favor, O God. In the abundance of your mercy, hear me, in the truth of your salvation.
Save me from the mire, so that I do not sink. Deliver me from those who hate me and from the deep waters.
Do not let the floodwaters overwhelm me, or the deep swallow me, or the pit close its mouth over me.
Hear me, Lord, for your mercy is good. In the abundance of your compassion, look upon me.
Do not turn your face away from your servant. Because I am in distress, hear me quickly.
Attend to my soul and redeem it. Deliver me because of my enemies.
For you know my reproach, my disgrace, and my shame. All who afflict me are before you.
My soul expected reproach and suffering. I waited for someone to grieve with me, but there was no one, and I found no one to comfort me.
They gave me gall for my food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
Let their table before them become a trap, and their reward a stumbling block.
Let their eyes be darkened so that they cannot see, and bend their backs down completely.
Pour out your anger upon them, and let the fury of your wrath seize them.
Let their dwelling be deserted, and let no one live in their tents.
For they persecuted the one you struck, and they did not add to the pain of my wounds.
Add lawlessness to their lawlessness, and do not let them enter into your righteousness.
Let them be erased from the books of the living, and let them not be recorded with the righteous.
I am poor and in pain. Your salvation, O God, has taken me in.
I will praise the name of my God with a song, and I will magnify him with praise.
This will please God more than a young bull growing horns and hooves.
Let the poor see and rejoice. Seek God, and your soul will live.
For the Lord has heard the poor, and he will not despise his prisoners.
Let heaven and earth praise him, the sea and everything that moves in it.
For God will save Zion, and the cities of Judah will be rebuilt. They will settle there and enjoy it.
The descendants of your servants will possess it, and those who love your name will rejoice in it.
For the end. A psalm of David, when the Lord saved him.
God, attend to my help; Lord, hurry to help me.
Let those who seek my life be ashamed and disgraced. Let those who wish me harm turn back and be ashamed.
Let those who say to me, “Well done! Well done!” turn back at once in shame.
Let all who seek you rejoice and be glad in you, Lord. Let those who love your salvation always say, “May the Lord be magnified!”
But I am poor and needy; God, help me. He is my helper and my defender; Lord my God, do not [?] delay.
Glory. Sessional hymn.
In you, Lord, I have placed my hope; let me never be put to shame.
In your righteousness deliver me and rescue me. Turn your ear toward me and save me.
Be a protecting God to me, and a strong place to save me, for you are my strength.
My God, deliver me from the hand of the sinner, from the hand of the lawbreaker and the oppressor.
For you are my endurance, Lord; Lord, you are my hope from my youth.
I have relied on you from the womb; from my mother’s womb you have been my protector. My song is always of you.
I have become a wonder to many, and you are my strong helper.
Let my mouth be filled with praise, so that I may praise your glory all day long, [?] your beauty.
Do not reject me at the time (not “at the time”) of old age; when my strength fails, do not abandon me.
For my enemies spoke to me, and those who watch for my life took counsel together,
saying, “God has abandoned him. Pursue him and seize him, for there is no one to rescue him.”
My God, do not be far from me; my God, attend to my help.
Let those who slander my soul be ashamed and perish. Let those who seek to harm me be clothed in shame and disgrace.
But I always hope in you, and every night I will add to your praise.
My mouth will proclaim your righteousness and your salvation all day long, for I have not known a scribe.
I entered in the Lord’s strength. Lord, I have remembered your righteousness, yours alone.
My God, [?] you taught me from my youth, and to this day I will proclaim your wonders.
Even into old age and advanced years, my God, do not abandon me, until I proclaim your arm to every generation to come—your power and your righteousness.
O God, to the highest heavens! You have done great things. O God, who is like you?
How many great and terrible troubles you have shown me! Yet you have brought me back to life, and long ago you brought me up from the depths of the earth.
You have increased your greatness toward me; you have brought me back to life, and again you have brought me up from the depths of the earth.
For I will praise you among the peoples, O Lord. With musical instruments I will praise your truth, O God; I will sing to you on the harp, O Holy One of Israel [?].
My lips will rejoice when I sing to you, and so will my soul, which you have redeemed.
My tongue, too, will meditate on your righteousness all day long, when those who seek to harm me are put to shame and disgrace.
A Psalm of David.
O God, give your judgment to the king, and your righteousness to the king’s son.
He will judge your people with righteousness and your poor with justice.
Let the mountains receive peace for their people, and the hills righteousness.
He will judge the poor among the people, save the children of the needy, and humble the slanderer.
He will endure with the sun, and before the moon, generation after generation.
He will come down like rain upon a fleece, like drops dripping onto the earth.
In his days righteousness will shine forth, and peace will abound until the moon is taken away.
He will rule from sea to sea, and from [?] to the ends of the inhabited world.
The Ethiopians will bow down before him, and his enemies will lick the dust.
The kings of Tarshish and the islands will bring gifts; the kings of Arabia and Sheba will bring gifts.
All the kings of the earth will bow down to him; all nations will serve him.
For he has rescued the poor from the powerful, and the needy who had no helper.
He will spare the poor and needy, and save the souls of the needy.
He will redeem their souls from usury and injustice, and his name will be honored among them.
He will live, and gold from Arabia will be given to him. They will pray to him continually and bless him all day long.
There will be stability on the earth, on the tops of the mountains. Its fruit will rise higher than Lebanon, and it will flourish out of the city like the grass of the earth.
May his name be blessed forever. His name endures before the sun. All the tribes of the earth will be blessed in him; all nations will call him blessed.
Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, who alone does wonders.
And blessed be his glorious name forever and ever. May the whole earth be filled with his glory. So be it, so be it.
Glory. A psalm of David.
How good God is to Israel, to those who are upright in heart.
But my feet had almost slipped; my steps had almost faltered.
For I envied the lawless when I saw the peace of sinners.
For there is no turning aside at their death, and there is firmness in their wounds.
They do not share in human troubles, and they will not suffer wounds along with other people.
Therefore pride held them fast to the end. They clothed themselves in their own injustice and impiety.
Their injustice will come out as if from fat. They have passed over to the desires of their hearts.
They thought and spoke in malice; they spoke injustice from on high.
They set their mouths against heaven, and their tongues ranged over the earth.
Therefore my people will return here, my people, and full days will be found among them.
And they said, “How does God know? Is there knowledge in the Most High?”
Look, these are the sinners who prosper; they have kept their wealth forever.
And I said, “In vain I made my heart righteous and washed my hands among the innocent.”
And I was struck all day long, and my reprover was there every morning.
If I said, “I will speak this way,” behold the generation of your sons, to whom I pledged myself.
And I thought I could understand. Look, my trouble is always before me,
until I enter God's sanctuary and understand what comes at the end.
Nevertheless, because of their deceit you appointed evils for them. You cast them down when they grew proud.
How suddenly they fell into desolation [?]! They came to an end and perished because of their lawlessness.
Like the dream of someone waking, Lord, in your city you will despise their images.
For my heart burned, and my inward parts were changed.
And I was brought low and did not understand. I was like a beast before you.
I am always with you. You have held my right hand.
You have guided me with counsel and received me with glory.
For what do I have in heaven? And what have I desired on earth besides you?
My heart and my flesh have failed. God is the God of my heart, and God is my portion forever.
For behold, those who go far from you will perish. [?] You have destroyed everyone who is unfaithful to you.
But for me it is good to cling to God, to place my hope in the Lord, so that I may proclaim all your praises in the gates of the daughter of Zion.
A Psalm of David.
Why, O God, have you rejected us forever? Why has your wrath blazed against the sheep of your pasture?
Remember your congregation, which you acquired from the beginning. He has redeemed the tribe of your inheritance, Mount Zion, where you have dwelt.
Raise your hands against their pride forever, against all the evil the enemy has done in your sanctuary.
Those who hate you boasted in the midst of your festival. They set up their signs as signs, and they did not know.
As at the way out above.
As in a forest of trees, they chopped apart its doors with axes. Together they demolished it with hatchet and pickaxe.
They set your sanctuary on fire. They desecrated the dwelling place of your name, bringing it to the ground.
Their kinsmen said together in their hearts, “Come, let us put an end to God's festivals in the land.”
We have not seen our signs. There is no longer a prophet, and he does not know us (us) [?].
How long, O Lord, will the enemy taunt you? Will the adversary provoke your name forever?
Why do you draw back your hand and your right hand from within your bosom (your bosom) forever?
But God is our king from before the ages; he has brought about salvation in the midst of the earth.
You made the sea firm by your power. You crushed the heads of the dragons in the water.
You shattered the dragon's head. You gave it as food to the Ethiopian people.
You broke open springs and streams. You dried up rivers in flood.
The day is yours, and the night is yours. You made the dawn and the sun.
You made all the boundaries of the earth. You created summer and spring.
Remember this: the enemy taunts the Lord, and foolish people have provoked your name.
Do not hand over to wild beasts the soul of those who praise you. Do not forget the souls of your poor forever.
Look upon your covenant, for the dark places of the earth are filled with houses of injustice.
Let the humble not turn back ashamed; the poor and needy will praise your name.
Arise, Lord, plead your cause. Remember the reproach directed against you by the fool all day long.
Do not forget the voice of those who pray to you. The pride of those who hate you rises continually.
Glory. A psalm of David.
I will give thanks to you, O God, I will give thanks, and we will call upon your name. I will recount all your wonders.
When I receive the appointed time, I will judge justly.
The earth and all who dwell on it melted away, but I established its pillars. Selah.
I said to the lawbreakers, “Do not break the law,” and to the sinners, “Do not lift up your horn.
Do not lift your horn on high, and do not speak injustice against God.”
For neither from the east nor from the west, nor from the deserted mountains,
for God is the judge: he humbles one and exalts another.
For in the Lord’s hand is a cup of unmixed wine, full of mixture. He poured from this cup into that one, but its dregs were not emptied out. The sinners of the earth will drink them.
But I will rejoice forever; I will sing to the God of Jacob.
I will break all the horns of sinners, but the horn of the righteous will be lifted up.
A psalm of David.
God is known in Judea; his name is great in Israel.
His place was in peace, and his dwelling in Zion.
There he shattered the strength of bows, the shield, weapons, and war.
You shine wondrously from the everlasting mountains.
All the foolish in heart will be thrown into confusion. They fell asleep in their sleep; all the men of wealth found nothing in their hands.
At your rebuke, O God of Jacob, all those mounted on horses fell asleep.
You are fearsome; who can stand against you once your anger begins?
From heaven you made your judgment heard. The earth was afraid and fell silent
when God arose for judgment, to save all the meek of the earth.
For human thought will praise [?] you, and the remainder of thought will praise you.
Make vows and fulfill them to the Lord our God. All who sit around him will bring gifts
to the fearsome one, who takes away the spirit of princes, who is more fearsome than the kings of the earth.
A Psalm of David.
With my voice I cried out to the Lord; with my voice I cried out to God, and he listened to me.
In the day of my distress I sought God. At night my hands were before him, and I was not deceived. My soul refused to be comforted.
I remembered God and rejoiced. In my afflictions my spirit grew faint.
My eyes were awake before the night watches. I was troubled and could not speak.
I thought about the days of old, and I remembered the ages long past and reflected.
At night I pondered in my heart, and my spirit searched:
Will the Lord reject us forever, and never again show favor?
Will he cut off your mercy completely? Will he bring his words to an end from generation to generation?
Will God forget to show mercy? Will he hold back your compassion in his anger?
And I said, “Now I have begun. This is the change of the right hand of the Most High.”
I remembered the Lord’s deeds, for I will remember your wonders from the beginning.
And I reflected on all your works, and I will ponder your deeds.
O God, your way is in the sanctuary. What god is as great as our God?
You are the God who works wonders. You have made your power known among the peoples.
With your arm you redeemed your people, the sons of Jacob and Joseph.
The waters saw you, O God; the waters saw you and were afraid. The depths were troubled by the mighty roar of the waters.
The clouds gave voice, for your arrows pass through.
The sound of your thunder was in the wheel. His lightning lit up the world. The earth saw, shook, and trembled.
Your way is in the sea, and your path is through the mighty waters, and your footprints cannot be known.
You led out your people like a sheep, [?] by the hand of Moses and Aaron. Glory. [?]
A Psalm of David.
Listen, my people; incline your ears to the words of my mouth.
I will open my mouth in parables; I will declare riddles from ancient times.
All that we have heard and understood, our fathers told us.
It was not hidden from their children in one generation, as they proclaimed the praises of the Lord and his power, and the wonders he performed.
He established a testimony in Jacob and laid down a law in Israel, which he commanded our fathers to make known to their sons,
so that another generation might know—the sons yet to be born—and they would rise and tell their own sons,
so that they would place their hope in God and not forget God's deeds, but seek his commandments,
so that they would not be like their fathers, a stubborn generation that provoked him to anger, a generation that did not set its heart right and whose spirit was not faithful to God.
The sons of Ephraim, drawing and shooting their bows, turned back on the day of [?].
They did not keep God's covenant and refused to walk in his law.
They forgot his kindness and the wonders he had shown them.
Before their fathers [?], he performed wonders in the land of Egypt, on the plain of Tanis. The name of the plain is Daneos.
He split the sea and led them through; the waters stood [?].
He led them out by a cloud during the day and all night by the light of fire.
He split a rock in the wilderness and gave them drink as in a vast waterless place [?].
He brought water out of the rock and brought it down like waters to him [?].
Yet they continued to sin, provoking the Most High to anger in the waterless land.
They tested God in their hearts by demanding food for themselves.
They spoke against God and said, “Can God prepare a table in the wilderness?
He struck the rock, and waters flowed and streams overflowed. But can he also give bread or prepare a table for his people?”
Therefore the Lord heard and was enraged; fire blazed up in Jacob, and anger rose against Israel,
because [?] they did not believe God or trust in his salvation.
He commanded the clouds above and opened the doors of heaven.
He rained manna upon them to eat and gave them heavenly bread.
Man ate the bread of angels; he sent them food in abundance.
He stirred up the south wind from heaven, and by his power brought in the west wind.
He rained flesh upon them like dust, and winged birds like the sand of the sea.
They fell in the midst of their camp, all around their dwellings.
They ate and were fully satisfied, and he brought them what they desired.
They were not deprived of what they desired; and while the food was still in their mouths,
God’s anger rose against them, and he killed many of them and brought down the chosen men of Israel.
Despite all this, they sinned again and did not believe in his wonders.
Their days came to an end in futility, and their years passed swiftly.
When he killed them, then they sought him; they turned back and came early to God.
They remembered that God was their helper [?], and that God Most High was their deliverer.
They loved him with their mouths, but lied to him with their tongues.
Their heart was not right with them, nor were they faithful to his covenant.
But he is merciful and will cleanse their sins and will not destroy them. He will repeatedly turn away his wrath and will not kindle all his sin [?].
He remembered that they were flesh, a breath that passes away and does not return.
How often they angered him in the wilderness and provoked him in the waterless land!
They turned back and put God to the test, and angered the Holy One of Israel.
They did not remember his hand, or the day when he delivered them from the hand of their oppressor,
How he set his signs in Egypt and his wonders in the plain of Tanis.
He turned their rivers into blood, and their rainwaters, so that they could not drink: rainwaters.
He sent dog flies against them, and they devoured them; and frogs destroyed them.
He gave their fruit to mildew—rust—and the produce of their labor to locusts.
He struck their vines with hail and their mulberry trees with frost.
He handed their livestock over to hail and their possessions to fire.
He sent upon them his furious anger, rage and anger and distress. He sent fierce angels against them.
He made a way, a path for his anger. He did not spare their souls from death, and he shut their livestock up in death.
And he struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, the firstfruits of all labor in the dwellings of Ham.
And he led his people out like sheep and brought them into the wilderness like a flock.
And he guided them in hope, and they were not afraid; and the sea covered their enemies.
And he brought them to the mountain of his sanctuary, this mountain which his right hand had acquired.
He drove out nations before them [?] and allotted the land to them by lot with a measuring cord; and he settled the tribes of Israel in their dwellings.
They tested and angered God Most High, and did not keep his decrees.
And they turned back and rebelled like their fathers; they became like a crooked bow.
And they angered him on their high places, and provoked him with their carved idols.
God heard and rejected them, and utterly despised Israel.
And he cast away the tabernacle at Shiloh, the dwelling where he had lived among human beings.
And he handed over their strength into captivity, and their splendor into the hands of enemies.
And he delivered his people over to the sword, and disregarded his inheritance.
Fire devoured their young men, and their maidens were not mourned.
Their priests fell by the sword, and their widows were not wept for.
And the Lord rose as though from sleep, like a mighty man shouting from wine.
And he struck their enemies back, and gave them everlasting disgrace.
And he rejected the dwelling of Joseph, and did not choose the tribe of Ephraim.
He chose the tribe of Judah, this mountain which he loved.
And he built his sanctuary like a unicorn; he established it on the earth forever.
He chose David his servant, and took him from the flocks of sheep.
He took him from the nursing ewes, to shepherd Jacob his servant and Israel his inheritance.
And he shepherded them with an innocent heart, and with the skill of your hands you guided them.
Glory. A psalm of Asaph.
O God, nations have entered your inheritance; they have defiled your holy temple; they have made Jerusalem like a storehouse for fruit.
They have made the corpses of your servants food for the birds of heaven, the flesh of your faithful ones food for the beasts of the earth.
They poured out their blood like water around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them.
We have become a disgrace to our neighbors, an object of mockery and ridicule to those around us.
How long, Lord? Will you be angry forever? Will your jealousy burn like fire?
Pour out your anger on the nations that do not know you, and on the kingdoms that have not called on your name.
For they have devoured Jacob and left his dwelling place deserted.
Do not remember our former sins. Let your mercies come quickly to meet us, Lord, for we have become utterly destitute.
Help us, God our Savior. For the glory of your name, Lord, rescue us, and cleanse our sins for your name’s sake.
Let the nations never say, “Where is their God?” Let vengeance for the shed blood of your servants be made known among the nations before our eyes.
Let the groaning of the prisoners come before you. By the greatness of your power, preserve the children of those who have been killed.
Repay our neighbors sevenfold into their laps the insults with which they insulted you, Lord.
But we, your people and the sheep of your pasture, will give thanks to you forever, God. From generation to generation we will proclaim your praise.
For the end. Concerning those who change. A testimony. A psalm of Asaph, concerning the Assyrian.
Shepherd of Israel, listen, you who lead Joseph like a sheep. You who sit upon the cherubim, reveal yourself
before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh. Stir up your power and come to save us.
God, restore us, and make your face shine, and we will be saved.
Lord God of hosts, how long will you be angry at the prayer of your servants?
You will feed us the bread of tears and give us tears to drink in measure.
You have made us an object of contention to our neighbors, and our enemies have mocked us.
Lord God of hosts, restore us, and make your face shine, and we will be saved.
You brought a vine out of Egypt. You drove out the nations and planted it.
You made a way before it and planted its root, and it filled the land.
Its shade covered the mountains, and its branches covered the cedars of God.
It stretched out its branches to the sea and its shoots to the river.
Why have you broken down its fence, so that everyone passing along the road plucks its fruit?
A boar from the forest has gnawed it, and a solitary wild beast has devoured it.
O God of hosts, restore us. Look down from heaven and see, and visit this vineyard of yours.
And make perfect what your right hand planted, and the son of man whom you made strong for yourself.
Burned with fire and dug up, they will perish at the rebuke of your face.
Let your hand be upon the man of your right hand, and upon the son of man whom you made strong for yourself.
And we will not turn away from you. You will give us life, and we will call upon your name.
O Lord God of hosts, restore us; [?] make your face shine, and we will be saved.
For the end. Concerning the winepresses. A psalm of Asaph. For the fifth day of the week [?].
Rejoice in God our helper. Let us shout to the God of Jacob.
Take up a psalm and beat the tambourine, the sweet-sounding lyre together with harps.
Blow the trumpet at the new moon, on the appointed day of your feast.
For this is a commandment for Israel and an ordinance of the God of Jacob.
He established it as a testimony for Joseph when he went out from the land of Egypt. He heard a language that I did not know.
He took their backs away from burdens. His hands labored at the basket.
In distress you called upon me, and I rescued you. I heard [?] in the hidden place of the storm. I tested you at the water of contention.
Listen, my people, and I will testify to you. O Israel, if only you would listen to me!
There shall be no other god among you, nor shall you bow down to a foreign god.
For I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.
But my people did not listen to my voice, and Israel paid no attention to me.
So I let them go according to the desires of their hearts. They will follow their own undertakings.
If my people had listened to me, if Israel had walked in my ways,
then I would have subdued their enemies with no effort, and I would indeed have laid my hand upon those who oppressed them.
The enemies of the Lord lied to him, and their time will last forever.
And [?] them with the finest wheat, and he satisfied them with honey from the rock.
Glory. A psalm of Asaph.
God stood in the assembly, and among the gods the Lord will judge.
How long will you judge unjustly and show favor to sinners?
Give justice to the orphan and the needy; uphold the rights of the lowly and the poor.
Rescue the poor and the needy; deliver him from the hands of sinners.
They neither knew nor understood; they walk in darkness. Let all the foundations of the earth be shaken.
I said, “You shall be gods, and all of you sons.”
But you die like human beings and will fall like one of the rulers.
Arise, Lord God, judge the earth, for you will inherit among all nations. [?]
A SONG FOR A PSALM OF ASAPH
God, who can compare with you? Do not remain silent or be still, God.
For look, your enemies have raised an uproar, and those who hate you have lifted up their heads.
They devised a cunning plan against your people and plotted against your holy ones.
They said, “Come, let us wipe them out from among the nations, so that the name of Israel will no longer be remembered.”
For [?] they plotted together with one mind; they made a covenant against you.
The tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites,
Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek, the Philistines, with those who live in Tyre.
For Assyria also joined them, and they became a support to the sons of Lot.
Do to them as you did to Midian and Sisera, and as you did to Jabin at the stream of Kishon.
They were destroyed at Endor and became like dung on the ground.
They made their rulers like Oreb and Zeeb, and Zebah and Zalmunna, and all their rulers,
who said, “Let us take possession of God's sanctuary for ourselves.”
My God, make them like a wheel, like dry stalks before the wind.
Like fire that burns the forests, like a flame that sets the mountains ablaze,
so you will burn them with your storm and throw them into confusion with your wrath.
Fill their faces with disgrace, and they will seek your name, Lord.
Let them be ashamed and thrown into confusion forever and ever; let them be disgraced and perish.
And they will know that your name is the Lord; you alone are the Most High over all the earth.
For the end. Concerning the winepresses. For the sons of Korah. A psalm.
How beloved are your dwelling places, Lord of hosts!
My soul longs and wastes away for the courts of the Lord. My heart and my flesh have rejoiced in the living God.
For the bird has found a home for itself, and the turtledove a nest for itself, where it has laid its young: your altars, Lord of hosts, my King and my God. Pause.
Blessed are those who dwell in your house; they will be praised forever and ever.
Blessed is the man whose help comes from you; he has set paths of ascent in his heart.
In the valley of weeping, in the place he appointed; for the lawgiver will give a blessing.
They will go from strength to strength, and the God of gods will appear in Zion.
Lord God of hosts, hear my prayer. Give ear, God of Jacob.
Look, God, our protector, and look upon the face of your anointed one.
For one day in your courts is better than a thousand. I have chosen to be an outcast in the house of my God rather than live in the dwellings of sinners.
For the Lord loves mercy and truth. God will give grace and strength. The Lord will not withhold good things from those who walk in innocence. [?]
Lord God of hosts, blessed is the man who trusts in you.
For the sons of Korah. A psalm of David.
You have shown favor to your land, Lord; you have brought back the captives of Jacob.
You have forgiven the lawless deeds of your people; you have covered all their sins.
You have restrained all your anger; you have turned away from your fierce wrath.
Turn us back, God of our salvation, and turn your wrath away from us.
Will you be angry with us forever? Will you extend your anger from generation to generation?
God, you will turn and give us life, and your people will rejoice in you.
Show us your mercy, Lord, and give us your salvation.
I will hear what the Lord God will say to me. [?] He will speak peace to your people and to his faithful ones and to those who turn their hearts toward him.
Indeed, his salvation is near those who fear him, so that your glory may dwell in our land.
Mercy and truth have met; righteousness and peace have kissed each other.
Truth has sprung up from the earth, and righteousness has looked down from heaven.
For the Lord will grant goodness, and our land will yield its fruit.
Righteousness will go before him and set its footsteps on the path.
Glory. Sessional hymn. A prayer of David.
Incline your ear, Lord, and hear me, for I am poor and needy.
Preserve my soul, for I am devout. My God, save your servant who trusts in you.
Have mercy on me, Lord, for I will cry to you all day long.
Gladden the soul of your servant, for to you, Lord, I have lifted up my soul.
For you, Lord, are good and gentle, and abundantly merciful to all who call upon you.
Listen to my prayer, Lord, and attend to the voice of my pleading.
In the day of my distress I cried to you, for you heard me.
There is none like you among the gods, Lord, nor are there any works like yours.
All the nations you have made will come and bow down before you, Lord, and glorify your name.
For you are great and work wonders; you alone are God.
Guide me, Lord, along your path, and I will walk in your truth. Let my heart rejoice in fearing your name.
I will give thanks to you, Lord my God, with all my heart, and I will glorify your name forever.
For great is your mercy toward me, and you have delivered my soul from the depths of Hades.
God, lawbreakers have risen against me, and an assembly of powerful men has sought my life. They have not set you before them.
But you, Lord my God, are compassionate and merciful, patient, abundantly merciful, and true.
Look upon me and have mercy on me. Give strength to your servant, and save the son of your maidservant.
Show me a sign of your favor, so that those who hate me may see it and be put to shame, for you, Lord, will help me and have comforted me.
For the sons of Korah. A psalm.
His foundations are on the holy mountains.
The Lord loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
Glorious things are spoken of you, city of God.
I will mention Rahab and Babylon to those who know me. Look, the foreigners, Tyre, and the people of Ethiopia—all these were there.
A man will say, “Mother Zion,” and a man was born in her, and the Most High himself founded her.
The Lord will tell in the books of the peoples and rulers who came to be in her.
The dwelling of all who rejoice is in you.
A song. For the sons [?]. A psalm. For the sons of Korah. For the end, concerning Mahalath, to answer. A word of understanding, by Heman the [?].
Lord, God of my salvation, I have cried out by day and by night before you.
Let my prayer come before you; incline your ear to my plea.
For my soul is filled with troubles, and my life has drawn near to Hades.
I was counted among those going down into the pit. I became like a man without help, free among the dead.
Like the slain who sleep in tombs, whom you remember no longer, and who have been cast away from your hand.
They placed me in the lowest pit, in dark places and in the shadow of death.
Your hand has pressed heavily upon me, and you have brought all your waves upon me.
You have removed my acquaintances far from me. They have made me an object of disgust to themselves. I was handed over and could not come out.
My eyes have grown weak from misery. I cried out to you, Lord, all day long; I stretched out my hands to you.
Will you work wonders for the dead? Or will physicians raise them up, and will they give thanks to you?
Will anyone tell of your mercy in the grave, or of your truth in destruction?
Will your wonders be known in darkness, or your righteousness in the land of forgetfulness?
But I have cried out to you, Lord, and in the morning my prayer will come before you. [?]
Why, Lord, do you reject the soul [?] and turn your face away from me?
I am poor and have been in hardship since my youth. Having been lifted up, I was humbled and troubled.
Your wrath has passed over me, and your terrors have troubled me.
They surrounded me like water all day long; together they closed in on me.
You have removed my close friend far from me, and my acquaintances because of suffering.
Glory. An instruction. Concerning the hidden things. By Ethan the [?].
I will sing of your mercy forever, Lord. From generation to generation I will proclaim your truth with my mouth.
For he said, “Mercy will be built up forever; your faithfulness will be established in the heavens.”
I made a covenant with my chosen ones; I swore to David my servant:
“I will establish your descendants forever, and I will build up your throne from generation to generation.”
The heavens will proclaim your wonders, Lord, and [?] your faithfulness in the assembly of the holy ones.
For who in the clouds can compare with the Lord? Who among the sons of God can be likened to the Lord?
O God, glorified in the council of the holy ones, he is great and feared above all those around him.
Lord God of hosts, who is like you? You are mighty, Lord, and your faithfulness surrounds you.
You rule the power of the sea; you still the surging of its waves.
You humbled the proud one like a wounded man; with your mighty arm you scattered your enemies.
The heavens are yours, and the earth is yours; you founded the inhabited world and its farthest reaches.
You created the north and the sea. Tabor and Hermon will rejoice in your name—that is, having heard the voice from heaven: “This is my beloved Son.”
Your arm is mighty. Let your hand be strengthened; let your right hand be raised high.
Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne; mercy and faithfulness will go before your face.
Blessed are the people who know the shout of joy. Lord, they will walk in the light of your face.
They will rejoice in your name all day long, and through your righteousness they will be exalted.
For you are the glory of their strength, and through your favor our horn will be raised high.
For protection belongs to the Lord and to the Holy One of Israel, our king.
Then you spoke in a vision of your sons and said, “I have placed help upon a mighty man; I have exalted one chosen from my people.
I found David my servant; with my holy oil I anointed him.
For my hand will help him, and my arm will strengthen him.
The enemy will have no success against us, and the son of lawlessness will no longer harm him.
I will cut down his enemies before him, and I will defeat those who hate him.
My faithfulness and my mercy are with him, and in my name his horn will be raised high.
I will set his hand upon the sea and his right hand upon the rivers.
He will call to me, ‘You are my Father, my God, the defender of my salvation.’
And I will make him the firstborn, exalted above the kings of the earth.
I will preserve my mercy for him forever, and my covenant will remain faithful to him.
And I will establish his descendants forever and ever, and his throne like the day and the heavens.
If his sons abandon my covenant and do not walk according to my judgments,
if they profane my statutes and do not keep my commandments,
I will punish their lawlessness with a rod, and the unrighteous with blows.
But I will not withdraw my mercy from them, nor will I wrong them in my faithfulness.
Nor will I profane my covenant, nor will I reject what comes from my lips.
Once I have sworn by my holiness: I will not lie to David.
His descendants will remain forever, and his throne will be like the sun before me.
And like the moon, established forever, and a faithful witness in heaven. Pause.
You have rejected and humiliated him; you have cast off your anointed one.
You have broken the covenant with your servant; you have profaned his sanctuary on the ground.
You have broken down all his defenses; you have put fear in his strongholds.
All who passed along the road were plundered; he became a reproach to his neighbors.
You have exalted the right hand of those who oppress him; you have made all his enemies rejoice.
You have turned away the help of his weapons and have not defended him in battle.
You have destroyed [?] from purification; you have cast his throne to the ground.
You have shortened the days of his life; you have covered him with shame.
How long, Lord, will you turn away completely? Will your anger blaze like fire? [?]
Remember what my existence is. Did you create all the sons of men in vain? — Substance.
Who is the person who will live and not see death? Will he deliver my soul from the hand of Hades?
Where are your mercies of old, Lord, which you swore to David in your faithfulness?
Remember, Lord, the reproach of your servants, which I have borne in my bosom, from many nations.
With it your enemies have reproached, Lord; with it they have reproached the change of your anointed one.
Blessed be the Lord forever. So be it, so be it.
Glory. A prayer of Moses, the man of God.
Lord, you have been our refuge from generation to generation.
Before the mountains came into being and the earth and the inhabited world were formed, from eternity to eternity, you are.
Do not turn a human being back to our humiliation. And you said, “Return, children of humankind.”
For a thousand years before your eyes, Lord, are like yesterday, which has passed, and like a watch in the night.
Their years will amount to nothing. In the morning they pass away like grass.
In the morning it flowers and passes away; toward evening it falls, grows hard, and withers.
For we have been consumed by your anger, and we have been shaken by your fury.
You have set our lawless deeds before you; our lifetime [?] in the light of your face.
For all our days have dwindled away, and we have been consumed by your anger. Our years were spent in meditation like a spider’s web.
The days [?] of our years number fifty years, or, if we have strength, eighty years; and what exceeds these is toil and pain. For gentleness has come upon us, and we shall be instructed.
Who knows the power of your anger, and your fury according to the fear of you?
Cleanse. Thus make your morning star known to me, and those whose hearts are bound in wisdom.
Return, Lord! How long? Be moved by the pleas of your servants.
In the morning we were filled with your mercy, Lord, and we rejoiced and were glad throughout all our days.
We were glad in return for the days when you humbled us, the years when we saw evil things.
And look upon your servants and upon your works, and guide their children.
And may the splendor of the Lord our God be upon us. Establish the works of our hands for us; establish the works of our hands.
Praise. A song of David.
Whoever lives under the protection of the Most High will dwell in the shelter of the God of heaven.
He will say to the Lord, “You are my defender and my refuge, my God; I trust in him.”
For he will deliver me from the hunter’s snare and from the troubling word.
He will overshadow you with his shoulders, and under his wings you will find hope. His truth will surround you like a shield.
You will not be afraid of terror by night or of the arrow that flies by day.
From the thing that passes through the darkness, from calamity and the noonday demon.
A thousand will fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right hand, but it will not come near you.
But with your own eyes you will look and see the repayment of sinners.
For you, Lord, are my hope. You have made the Most High your refuge.
Evil will not come to you, and no plague will approach your body.
For he will command his angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways.
They will lift you up in their hands, so that you never strike your foot against a stone.
You will tread upon the asp and the basilisk, and trample the lion and the serpent.
Because he has put his hope in me, I will deliver him; I will shelter him because he has known my name.
He will call upon me, and I will hear him. I am with him in trouble; I will rescue him and glorify him.
I will satisfy him with length of days and show him my salvation.
Glory. Sessional hymn. A psalm. A song for the Sabbath day.
It is good to give thanks to the Lord and to sing to your name, Most High,
To proclaim your mercy in the morning [?] and your truth every night,
On a ten-stringed psaltery, with a song on the harp.
For you have shown me favor, Lord, through your creation, and I will rejoice in the works of your hands.
How great your works have become, Lord! Your thoughts have become very deep.
A senseless man does not know, and a foolish man does not understand these things.
When sinners spring up like grass and all who practice lawlessness flourish, it is so that they may be destroyed forever and ever.
But you, Lord, are the Most High forever.
For look, your enemies, Lord—for look, your enemies will perish, and all who practice lawlessness will be scattered.
My horn will rejoice like that of a unicorn, and my old age will be rich with oil.
My eye has looked upon my enemies, and my ear will hear those who rise against me and do evil.
The righteous man will flourish like a palm tree and grow like a cedar in Lebanon.
Those planted [?] in the Lord’s house will flourish in the courts of the house of our God.
They will still flourish in old age and will be well nourished and [?].
To proclaim that the Lord our God is upright, and there is no injustice in him.
Of David. A song of praise, for the first day of the week, when the earth was inhabited.
The Lord reigns; he has clothed himself in majesty. The Lord has clothed himself in strength and girded himself. For he has established the world, which will not be shaken.
Your throne has been established from that time; you are from eternity.
The rivers will rise up, Lord; the rivers will raise their voices; the rivers will raise their waves.
Above the sound of many waters, the surges of the sea are wondrous; the Lord on high is wondrous.
Your testimonies have proved utterly trustworthy. Holiness befits your house, Lord, for all time.
A psalm of David, for the fourth day of the week.
The Lord is a God of vengeance; the God of vengeance has acted openly.
Rise up, judge of the earth; repay the proud what they deserve.
How long will sinners, Lord, how long will sinners boast?
They speak out and utter injustice; all who practice lawlessness speak out.
They have humbled your people, Lord, and afflicted your inheritance.
They have put the widow and the orphan to death, and killed the foreigner.
And they said, “The Lord will not see, nor will the God of Jacob understand.”
Understand now, you senseless among the people! You fools, when will you become wise?
Will he who planted the ear not hear? Will he who formed the eye not [?]?
Will he who disciplines the nations not rebuke—he who teaches human beings knowledge?
The Lord knows human thoughts, that they are futile.
Blessed is the man whom you discipline, Lord, and teach from your law,
So that you may give us relief from evil days, until a pit is dug for the sinner.
For the Lord will not reject his people, nor will he abandon his inheritance,
Until righteousness returns to judgment, and [?] it, all the upright in heart.
Who will rise up for me against evildoers? Or who will stand with me against those who practice lawlessness?
If the Lord had not helped me, my soul would soon have settled in Hades.
Whenever I said, “My foot is slipping,” your mercy, Lord, helped me.
When the sorrows in my heart multiplied, your consolations brought joy to my soul.
Let the throne of lawlessness, which creates hardship by decree, not remain with you.
He will hunt down the sinner’s soul and condemn innocent blood.
The Lord became my refuge, and my God became the support of my hope.
The Lord will repay them for their lawlessness, and the Lord our God will destroy them for their wickedness.
Glory. A song of David.
Come, let us rejoice in the Lord; let us shout joyfully to God our Savior.
Let us come into his presence with thanksgiving, and shout joyfully to him with psalms.
For the Lord is a great God, a great king over all the earth.
For the ends of the earth are in his hand, and the mountain heights are his.
For the sea is his, and he made it, and his hands formed the dry land.
Come, let us worship and fall down before him, and let us weep before the Lord who made us.
For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hands. Today, if you hear his voice,
do not harden your hearts as in the provocation, as on the day of testing in the wilderness,
where your fathers tested me; they tested me and saw my works.
For forty years I was indignant with that generation, and I said, “They always stray in their hearts, and they have not understood my ways.”
So I swore in my anger, “They shall not enter my rest.”
When the temple was built [?]. A psalm of David.
Sing a new song to the Lord; sing to the Lord, all the earth.
Sing to the Lord and bless his name; proclaim the good news of his salvation day after day.
Declare his glory among the nations, his wonders among all peoples.
For the Lord is great and greatly to be praised; he is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the nations are demons, but the Lord made the heavens.
Praise and beauty are before him; his works are holy, and majesty is in his sanctuary.
Bring the Lord glory, you families of nations; bring the Lord glory and honor.
Bring the Lord the glory of his name; take offerings and enter his courts.
Bow down to the Lord in his holy court; let all the earth tremble before him.
Say among the nations that the Lord reigns. For he has established the world, which will not be shaken. He will judge the peoples with justice.
Let the heavens rejoice and the earth be glad; let the sea and everything in it stir.
The fields and everything in them will rejoice. Then all the trees of the forest will rejoice
before the Lord, for he is coming, for he will come to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with your truth.
A Psalm of David, when his land was established.
The Lord reigns; let the earth rejoice, and let the many islands be glad.
Cloud and darkness surround him; righteousness and judgment fill his throne.
Fire will go ahead and burn up his enemies all around.
His lightning lit up the world; [?] the earth saw and trembled.
The mountains melted like wax before the Lord, before the Lord of all the earth.
The heavens proclaimed his righteousness, and all the peoples saw his glory.
Let all who bow down to carved images be put to shame, [?] those who boast of their idols. Bow down to him, all his angels.
Zion heard and was glad, and the daughters of Judah rejoiced because of your judgments, Lord.
For you, Lord, are the Most High over all the earth; you are exalted far above all gods.
You who love the Lord, hate evil. The Lord guards the souls of his faithful ones; he will rescue them from the hands of sinners.
Light has dawned for the righteous, and gladness for the upright in heart.
Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous, and give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness.
Glory. A Psalm of David.
Sing a new song to the Lord, for the Lord has done wonderful things. His right hand and his holy arm are his salvation.
The Lord made his salvation known among the nations and revealed his righteousness.
He remembered his mercy toward Jacob and his faithfulness toward the house of Israel. All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
Shout to the Lord, all the earth! Sing, rejoice, and sing praises!
Sing to our God with harps and with the sound of a psalm.
With metal trumpets and the sound of a horn, shout before the King and Lord (and Lord).
Let the sea and all that fills it be moved, the world and all who live in it.
The rivers will clap their hands together; the mountains will rejoice before the Lord, for he is coming.
For he will come to the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with fairness.
A PSALM OF DAVID.
The Lord reigns; let the peoples rage. He sits upon the cherubim; let the sea be shaken.
The Lord is great in Zion and exalted above all peoples.
Let them give thanks to your great name, for it is fearsome and holy.
The king's honor loves justice. You have established fairness; you have carried out justice and righteousness in Jacob.
Exalt the Lord our God and bow down at his footstool, for he is holy.
Moses and Aaron were among his priests, and Samuel among those who called upon his name. They called upon him, the Lord, and he heard them.
He spoke to them in a pillar of cloud, because they kept his testimonies and the commandments that he gave us.
O Lord our God, you heard them. You were a merciful God to them, and took vengeance [?] for all their deeds.
Exalt the Lord our God and bow down on his holy mountain, for the Lord our God is holy.
A PSALM OF DAVID. THANKSGIVING.
Shout to God, all the earth!
Serve the Lord with gladness. Come before him with joy.
Know that the Lord is our God. You made us, and we did not make ourselves. We are his people and the sheep of his pasture.
Enter his gates with thanksgiving and his courts with songs. Give thanks to him and praise his name.
For the Lord is good; his mercy endures forever, and his faithfulness from generation to generation.
A PSALM OF DAVID.
I sing of mercy and justice to you, O Lord.
I will sing and gain understanding in the blameless way. When will you come to me? I walked with an innocent heart within my house.
I did not set unlawful things before my eyes. I hated those who committed transgression.
A deceitful heart did not cling to me; I did not know the wicked person who turned away from me.
I drove out anyone who secretly slandered his neighbor. I would not eat with anyone who had a proud eye and an insatiable heart.
My eyes were on the faithful of the land, to seat them with me. Anyone who walked a blameless path served me.
Anyone who practiced arrogance did not live within my house; anyone who spoke unjust things did not stand upright before my eyes.
Each morning I killed all the sinners of the land, to remove from the Lord’s city all who practiced lawlessness.
Glory. A prayer of the poor person when he grows faint and pours out his prayer before God.
Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to you.
Do not turn your face away from me. On the day I am in distress, incline your ear toward [?]. On the day (I am in distress) I call to you, hear me quickly.
For my days have vanished like smoke, and my bones have dried up like dry wood.
I was struck down like grass; my heart withered, for I forgot to eat my bread.
Because of the sound of my groaning, my bones clung to my flesh.
I became like a pelican in the wilderness; I was like an owl on [?].
I kept watch and became like a bird sitting alone on a roof.
All day my enemies taunted me; those who boasted swore by me.
For I ate ashes like bread and mixed my drink with weeping.
Because of your anger and your fury, for you lifted me up and cast me down.
My days faded like a shadow, and I withered like grass.
But you, Lord, remain forever, and your memory endures from generation to generation.
You will arise and have mercy on Zion, for it is time to have mercy on her; the time has come.
For your servants have cherished her stones, and they will show tenderness toward her dust.
The nations will fear the Lord’s name, and all the kings of the earth will fear your glory.
For the Lord will rebuild Zion and appear in his glory.
He looked upon the prayer of his humble ones and did not despise their supplication.
Let these things be written for another generation, and a people to be created will praise the Lord.
For he looked down from his holy height; the Lord looked from heaven upon the earth,
to hear the groaning of the prisoners and to release those condemned to death,
to proclaim the Lord’s name in Zion and to praise him in Jerusalem,
when the peoples gather together, and kings serve the Lord.
He answered him in the course of his strength: “Tell me how few my days are.
Do not take me away halfway through my days; your years endure from generation to generation.
In the beginning, [?], Lord, you laid the earth’s foundation, and the heavens are the work of your hands.
They will perish, but you will remain. They will all wear out like a garment, and you will roll them up like a cloak, and they will be changed.
But you are the same, and your years will never end.
The children of your servants will dwell securely, and their descendants will be established forever.”
A psalm. [?] Of David.
Bless the Lord, my soul, and let everything within me bless his holy name.
Bless the Lord, my soul, and do not forget all his benefits.
He forgives all your lawless deeds and heals all your diseases.
He redeems your life from decay and crowns you with mercy and compassion.
He satisfies your desire with good things; your youth will be renewed like an eagle’s.
The Lord acts mercifully and gives justice to all who are oppressed.
He made his ways known to Moses and his purposes to the children of Israel.
The Lord is compassionate and merciful, patient and abundantly merciful.
He will not remain angry to the end, nor will he be hostile forever.
You have not dealt with us according to our lawless deeds, nor have you repaid us according to our sins.
For as high as heaven is above the earth, the Lord has made his mercy strong toward those who fear him.
As far as the east is from the west, he has removed our lawless deeds from us.
As a father has compassion on his children, so the Lord will have compassion on those who fear him.
For he knows how we were made, and he has remembered that we are dust.
A person's days are like grass; like a flower of the field, so he blooms.
For a breath passes through him, and he is gone, and he will no longer know his place.
But the Lord's mercy is from everlasting to everlasting upon those who fear him, and his righteousness upon their children's children,
who keep his covenant and remember his commandments to carry them out.
The Lord has established his throne in heaven, and his kingdom rules over all.
Bless the Lord, all his angels, mighty in strength, who carry out his word, listening to the voice of his words.
Bless the Lord, all his hosts, and his servants who do his will.
Bless the Lord, all his works, and in every place under his dominion.
Glory. A psalm of David, concerning the creation of the whole world.
Bless the Lord, my soul. O Lord my God, you have become exceedingly great. You have clothed yourself in praise and beauty,
wrapping yourself in light as in a garment, stretching out heaven like a hide.
He covers his upper chambers with water, makes the clouds his means of travel, and walks on the wings of the wind.
He makes his angels spirits and his servants a burning fire.
He establishes the earth on its firm foundation; it will not be moved forever and ever.
The deep is its covering, like a garment; the waters will stand upon the mountains.
At your rebuke they will flee, and at the sound of your thunder they will be afraid.
Mountains rise and plains descend to the place you established.
You set a boundary that they will not cross, nor will they return to cover the earth.
He sent springs into the valleys; the waters will flow between the mountains.
They will give drink to every beast of the meadow, and wild donkeys wait in their thirst.
Beside them the birds of heaven dwell; from among the rocks they will raise their voices.
He waters the mountains from his upper chambers; the earth will be satisfied with the fruit of your works.
He makes pasture grow for livestock and plants for people's use, to bring forth bread from the earth,
and wine will gladden the human heart, to make the face shine with oil, and bread will strengthen the human heart.
The trees of the fields will be satisfied, and the cedars of Lebanon, which you [?].
There the birds will nest; the heron's dwelling rules over them.
The high mountains are for the deer; the rocks are a refuge for the hares.
You made the moon to mark the seasons, and the sun knows its setting.
You appointed darkness, and night came; in it every beast of the forest will roam.
The young lions roar to seize prey and ask God for their food.
The sun rose, and they gathered together; they will lie down in their dens.
A person goes out to his work and to his labor until evening.
How great your works have become, Lord! You made them all with wisdom; the earth is filled with your creation.
And here is the great, wide sea; there are creeping creatures beyond number, living creatures both small and great.
There ships sail across, and the dragon you created to play with.
All look to you to give them their food at the proper time.
When you give to them, they will gather; when you open your hand, [?] with every good thing.
When you turn your face away, they will be troubled. You will take away their breath, and they will perish and return to their dust.
You will send forth your Spirit, and they will be created; you will renew the face of the earth.
May the glory of the Lord endure forever; the Lord will rejoice in his works.
He looks upon the earth and makes it tremble; he touches the mountains, and they smoke.
I will sing to the Lord throughout my life; I will sing praise to my God as long as I exist.
May my words be pleasing to him, and I will rejoice in the Lord.
Sinners will vanish from the earth, and the lawless will cease to exist. Bless the Lord, my soul.
GLORY. ALLELUIA.
Give thanks to the Lord and call upon his name; make his deeds known among the nations.
Sing to him and sing praises to him; tell of all his wonders.
Glory in his holy name; let the hearts of those who seek the Lord rejoice.
Seek the Lord and be strengthened; seek his face always.
Remember the wonders he has done, his marvels and the judgments of his mouth.
Descendants of Abraham, his servants, sons of Jacob, his chosen ones!
He is the Lord our God; his judgments are throughout the earth.
He remembered his covenant forever, the word he commanded for a thousand generations,
which he established with Abraham, and his oath to Isaac.
He established it as a decree for Jacob, as an everlasting covenant for Israel,
saying, “To you I will give the land of Canaan as your allotted inheritance.”
For they were few in number, only a few foreigners living in it.
They went from nation to nation, and from a kingdom to another people.
He allowed no one to oppress them, and he rebuked kings on their behalf:
“Do not touch my anointed ones [?], and do not act wickedly against my prophets.”
He called down a famine upon the land; he destroyed every supply of bread.
He sent a man ahead of him: Joseph was sold as a slave.
They humbled his feet in fetters; iron pierced his soul,
until his word came to pass; the Lord’s word tested him by fire.
The king sent and released him; the ruler of the people set him free.
He appointed him lord over his house and ruler over all his possessions,
so that he might teach his princes to be like himself and make his elders wise.
Israel entered Egypt; Jacob lived as a foreigner in the land of Ham.
He greatly increased [?] his people and made them stronger than their enemies.
He turned his own heart to hate his people and to deal deceitfully with his servants.
He sent Moses his servant, and Aaron, whom he had chosen for himself.
He placed among them the words of his signs and of his wonders in the land of Ham.
He sent darkness, and it grew dark, because they had defied his words.
He turned their waters into blood; the sea [?]. He killed their fish.
Their land teemed with frogs, even in the kings’ chambers.
He spoke, and dog flies came, and gnats throughout all their territory.
He turned their rain into hail, burning fire in their land.
