He struck their vineyards and their fig trees; he shattered every tree in their territory.
He spoke, and locusts and caterpillars came, beyond counting.
They ate every plant in their land and devoured all the produce of their land.
He killed every firstborn of theirs in their land, the first fruits of all their labor.
He brought them out with silver and gold, and there was no one sick in their tribe.
Egypt will rejoice at its own departure, for fear of them fell upon them.
He will spread clouds as their covering, and fire to give them light at night.
They asked, and quails came, and he satisfied them with bread from heaven.
He split open a rock, and waters flowed; rivers flowed through waterless places.
For he remembered his holy word, which he had given to Abraham his servant.
He brought out his people with joy, his chosen ones with gladness.
He placed them in the lands of the nations, and they inherited the labor of the peoples.
So that they might keep his statutes and seek his law.
Glory. Sessional hymn. Alleluia.
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy lasts forever.
Who can recount the mighty deeds of the Lord or make all his praise heard?
Blessed are those who uphold justice and do what is right at all times.
Remember me, Lord, when you show favor to your people; visit us with your salvation.
To see the prosperity of your chosen ones. Rejoice in the joy of your nation, and boast with your inheritance.
We have sinned with our fathers; we have acted lawlessly and have not acted justly.
Our fathers in Egypt did not understand your wonders. They did not remember the abundance of your mercy, and they provoked you to anger at the departure into the Red Sea.
And he saved himself for the sake of your name, to show them your power.
He rebuked the Red Sea, and it dried up. He led them through the waterless place as through a desert [?].
And he saved [?] from the hands of those who hated them; he delivered them from the hands of their enemies.
The water covered those who oppressed them; not one of them escaped.
And they believed his word and sang his praise.
They quickly forgot his deeds; they did not wait for his counsel.
They craved intensely in the wilderness and put God to the test in the waterless land.
And he gave them what they asked for and sent satisfaction to their souls.
And they angered Moses [?] in the camp, and Aaron, the Lord’s holy one.
The earth opened and swallowed Dathan, and covered the gatherings of Abiram.
And a fire blazed in their assembly; a flame burned up the sinners.
And they made a calf at Horeb and worshiped the cast image.
You will exchange his glory for the image of a calf that eats hay.
And they forgot God, who saved them, who had done great things in Egypt,
wonders in the land of Ham, and fearsome things at the Red Sea.
And he said, “Let me destroy them”—had not Moses, his chosen one, stood in the breach before him to turn back his wrath, so that he would not destroy them.
And they despised the desirable land and did not believe his words.
And they grumbled in their tents; they did not listen to the Lord’s voice.
And he raised his hand against [?], to strike them down in the wilderness,
and to strike down their descendants among the nations and scatter them among the lands.
And they joined themselves to Baal-peor and ate sacrifices offered to the dead.
And they provoked him by their deeds (their own), and death spread among them.
And Phinehas stood up and made atonement, and the slaughter stopped.
And it was counted (to him was) to him as righteousness, from generation to generation forever.
And they angered him at the water of contention, and Moses suffered because of them.
For they provoked his spirit, and he spoke rashly with his lips.
They did not destroy the nations that the Lord had told them to destroy.
And they humbled themselves among the nations and learned their deeds.
And they served their idols, and this became a snare to them.
And they sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons.
And they shed innocent blood, the blood of their sons and daughters, whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan; and the land was slain by bloodshed.
And it was defiled by their deeds, and they committed adultery in their undertakings.
And the Lord became fiercely angry with his people, and he abhorred his own inheritance.
And he handed them over to their enemies, and those who hated them ruled over them.
And their enemies oppressed them, and they were humbled under their hands.
Many times he delivered them, but they [?] by their own counsel, and they were brought low through their lawlessness.
And the Lord saw when they were distressed, and he heard their prayer.
And he remembered his covenant and relented according to the abundance of his mercy.
And he granted them mercy before all who had taken them captive.
Save us, O Lord our God, and gather us from among the nations, so that we may give thanks to your holy name and glory in your praise.
Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Let all the people say, “So be it.”
Glory. 105. Alleluia.
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
Let those redeemed by the Lord say so, whom he redeemed from the enemy’s hand.
And he gathered them from the lands, from the east and the west, from the north and the sea.
They wandered in a waterless wilderness; they found no way to an inhabited city.
Hungry and thirsty, [?].
And they cried out to the Lord when they were distressed, and he delivered them from their troubles.
And he led them along a straight path, so that they could enter an inhabited city.
Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercy and for his wonders for humankind.
For he has satisfied the empty soul and filled the hungry soul with good things.
Those who sat in darkness and in the shadow of death, bound in poverty and iron.
Because they defied the words of God and spurned the counsel of the Most High.
And their hearts were humbled by hardships; they grew weak, and there was no one to help.
And they cried out to the Lord when they were in distress, and he saved them from their troubles.
He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death, and tore their bonds apart.
Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercy and for his wonders for humankind.
For he shattered the bronze gates and broke the iron bars.
He received them from the path of their lawlessness, for they were humbled because of their own lawless deeds.
Their souls loathed every kind of food, and they drew near to the gates of death.
And they cried out to the Lord when they were in distress, and he delivered them from their troubles.
He sent his word and healed them, and delivered them from their destruction.
Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercy and for his wonders for humankind.
And let them offer him a sacrifice of praise and proclaim his works with joy.
Those who go down to the sea in ships, doing business on the mighty waters—
They saw the works of the Lord and his wonders in the deep.
He spoke, and a stormy wind arose, and the waves rose high.
They rise to the heavens and descend to the depths; their souls melt away in their misery.
They were thrown into confusion and staggered like drunken people, and all their wisdom was swallowed up.
And they cried out to the Lord when they were in distress, and he brought them out of their troubles.
And he commanded the storm to become calm, and its waves fell silent.
And they rejoiced because the waves fell silent, and he guided them to their desired harbor.
Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercy and for his wonders for humankind.
And let them exalt him in the assembly of the people and praise him in the council of the elders.
He turned rivers into a wilderness and springs of water into thirsty ground;
Land [?] into [?], because of the wickedness of those living on it.
You turned the wilderness into pools of water, and waterless land into springs of water.
And he settled the hungry there [?], and established cities to live in.
And they sowed fields and planted vineyards, and produced a harvest of grain.
And he blessed them, and they multiplied greatly; he did not diminish their livestock.
And they dwindled and suffered oppression through sorrow, evils, and sickness.
Contempt was poured out upon their princes, and he made them wander through trackless country, where there was no path.
And he helped the poor out of poverty, and made their families like flocks of sheep.
The upright will see and rejoice, and all lawlessness will shut its mouth.
Who is wise and will guard himself, and will understand the Lord’s mercies?
GLORY. SONGS [?].
My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready. I sing and will sing praise to my glory.
Awake, my glory! Awake, psaltery and harp! I will rise early.
I will give thanks to you among the peoples, O Lord; I will sing praise to you among the nations.
For your mercy has grown great as far as the heavens, and your truth reaches to the clouds.
Be exalted above the heavens, O God, and let your glory be over all the earth.
So that your beloved may give thanks, save with your right hand and hear me.
God has spoken in his holy place: “I will rejoice and divide Shechem, and measure out the valley of [?].
Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine; Ephraim is the protection of my head; Judah is my king.
Moab is the pot of my hope; over Edom I will stretch out my shoe. Foreigners have submitted to me.”
Who will bring me into the besieged city? Who will guide me as far as Edom?
Is it not you, O God, who rejected us? And will you not go out, O God, with our armies?
Give us help against affliction, for human deliverance is vain.
With God we will act mightily, and he will bring our enemies to nothing.
FOR THE END. A PSALM OF DAVID.
O God of my praise, do not remain silent.
For the mouth of a sinner and a deceitful mouth have opened against me. They have spoken against me with a deceitful tongue.
They surrounded me with hateful words and fought against me [?].
In return for my love, they slandered me, but I devoted myself to prayer.
They repaid me with evil for good and with hatred for my love.
Appoint a sinner over him, and let the devil stand at his right hand.
When he is judged, let him come away condemned, and let his prayer be counted as sin.
Let his days be few, and let another take his office.
Let his sons be fatherless and his wife a widow.
Let his sons wander and move from place to place, and [?], and let them be driven from their homes.
Let the creditor search out everything he owns, and let strangers plunder the fruits of his labor.
Let him have no defender, and let there be no one to show mercy to his fatherless children.
Let his children perish; let his name be wiped out within one generation.
Let the lawlessness of his heart be remembered before the Lord, and let his mother's sin not be blotted out.
Let them always be before the Lord, and let their memory be wiped from the earth.
For he did not remember to show mercy, but persecuted a poor and needy man, seeking to kill one whose heart was broken.
He loved cursing, and it came upon him; he did not desire blessing, and it went far from him.
He clothed himself in cursing as in a robe, and it entered his body like water and his bones like oil.
Let it be to him like a robe he wears, and like a belt he always fastens around himself.
This is the work of those who slander me, Lord, and of those who speak evil against my soul.
But you, Lord, Lord, act on my behalf for your name's sake, for his mercy is good.
Deliver me, for I am poor and needy, and my heart is troubled within me.
I am taken away like a fading shadow; I am shaken off like locusts.
My knees have grown weak from fasting, and my flesh has changed for lack of oil.
I became an object of scorn to them; when they saw me, they shook their heads.
Help me, Lord my God, and save me [?] your mercy.
Let them know that this is your hand and that you, Lord, have done this.
They will curse you, but you will bless. Those who rise against us will be put to shame, but your servant will rejoice.
Those who slander me will be clothed in shame; they will wrap themselves in their disgrace as in a garment.
I will give great thanks to the Lord with my mouth, and I will praise him among the multitude.
For he stood at the poor man's right hand, to save [?] from those who pursue my soul.
Glory. Sitting.
The Lord said to my lord, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for my feet.”
The Lord will send you a scepter of power from Zion, and you will prevail among your enemies.
Dominion is with you on the day of your power, in the splendor of your holy ones. From the womb, before the morning star, I begot you.
The Lord has sworn and will not change his mind: “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.”
The Lord at your right hand has crushed kings on the day of your [?].
He will judge the nations; he will fill them with fallen bodies. He will crush the heads of many on the earth.
He will drink from a stream along the way; therefore he will lift up his head.
Alleluia.
I will give thanks to you, Lord, with all my heart, in the council of the upright and in the assembly.
The Lord's works are great, sought out in all his purposes.
Praise and majesty are his, and his righteousness endures forever.
He has made his wonders remembered. The Lord is merciful.
He has given food to those who fear him. He will remember his covenant forever.
He will proclaim the might of his works to his people, to give them the inheritance of the nations.
The works of his hands are truth and justice; all his commandments are trustworthy.
They are established forever and ever, made in truth and righteousness.
He sent deliverance to his people; he ordained his covenant forever. His name is holy and awe-inspiring.
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. All who practice it have good understanding. His praise endures forever and ever.
Alleluia.
Blessed is the man who fears the Lord; he will take great delight in his commandments.
His name will be mighty on earth; the generation of the upright will be blessed.
Glory and wealth are in his house, and his righteousness endures forever.
Light will dawn in the darkness for the upright; he is merciful, compassionate, and righteous.
A good man shows mercy and gives; he will consider his words in judgment.
For he will never be shaken; the righteous man will be remembered forever.
He will not fear bad news; his heart is ready to trust in the Lord.
His heart is firmly established; he will not be shaken until he looks upon his enemies.
He distributes and gives to the poor; his righteousness endures forever and ever. His horn will be lifted up in glory.
The sinner will see and become angry; he will gnash his teeth and waste away. The desire of sinners will perish.
GLORY.
Praise the Lord, you servants; praise the name of the Lord.
Blessed be the name of the Lord, from now and forever.
From the rising of the sun to its setting, the name of the Lord is to be praised.
The Lord is high above all nations; his glory is above the heavens.
Who is like the Lord our God, who dwells on high
and looks upon the lowly things in heaven and on earth?
He raises the poor from the earth and lifts the needy from the dung heap,
to seat him with princes, with the princes of his people.
He settles the barren woman in a home as a mother rejoicing in her children.
ALLELUIA.
When Israel went out of Egypt, the house of Jacob from a people of foreign speech,
Judah became his sanctuary, Israel his dominion.
The sea saw and fled; the Jordan turned back.
The mountains skipped like rams, and the hills like lambs of the flock.
What is wrong with you, sea, that you fled, and with you, Jordan, that you turned back?
Let the mountains leap like rams, and the hills like lambs of the flock.
The earth trembled before the Lord, before the God of Jacob,
who turns rock into pools of water and flint into a spring of water.
Not to us, Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory, because of your mercy and your truth.
Why should the nations ever say, “Where is their God?”
But our God is in heaven and on earth, and he has done everything he wished [?].
The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of human hands.
They have mouths but do not speak; they have eyes but do not see.
They have ears but do not hear; they have nostrils but do not smell.
They have hands but do not feel; they have feet but do not walk; and they make no sound with their throats.
May those who make them become like them, and all who trust in them.
The house of Israel trusted in the Lord; he is their helper and protector.
The house of Aaron trusted in the Lord; he is their helper.
Those who fear the Lord trusted in the Lord; he is their helper and defender.
The Lord remembered us and blessed us. He has blessed the house of Israel; he has blessed the house of Aaron.
He has blessed those who fear the Lord, the small together with the great.
May the Lord increase you and your children.
You are blessed by the Lord, who made heaven and earth.
The heaven of heavens belongs to the Lord, but he gave the earth to the children of humankind.
The dead will not praise you, Lord, nor will any who go down into Hades.
But we who are alive will bless the Lord, from now and forever.
ALLELUIA.
I have loved, because the Lord heard the voice of my supplication.
And throughout my days I will call upon him.
The pains of death surrounded me; the perils of Hades found me. I found trouble and pain.
I will call on the name of the Lord: O Lord, deliver my soul.
The Lord is merciful and righteous, and our God shows mercy.
The Lord protects infants. I was brought low, and he saved me.
Return, my soul, to your rest, for the Lord has done good to you.
For he has delivered my soul from death, my eyes from tears, and my feet from slipping.
I will be pleasing before the Lord in the land of the living.
GLORY. ALLELUIA.
I believed, therefore I spoke. But I was brought very low.
I said in my dismay, “Everyone is a liar.”
What shall I give back to the Lord for all that he will give us?
I will take the cup of salvation and call on the name of the Lord.
I will fulfill my vows to the Lord before all his people.
Precious before the Lord is the death of his holy ones.
O Lord, I am your servant, [?] your servant and the son of your maidservant. I break my bonds.
And I will offer you a sacrifice of praise, and I will call on the name of the Lord.
I will fulfill my vows to the Lord before all his people,
in the courts of the Lord’s house, in your midst, Jerusalem.
ALLELUIA.
Praise the Lord, all nations; praise him, all peoples.
For his mercy toward us has grown strong, and the truth of the Lord endures forever.
ALLELUIA.
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
Let the house of Israel now say that he is good.
Let the house of Aaron now say that he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
Let all who fear the Lord now say that he is good, for [?]
In my distress I called on the Lord, and he answered me in a spacious place.
The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what anyone can do to me.
The Lord is my helper, and I will look upon my enemies.
It is better for me to trust in the Lord than to trust in a human being.
It is better to put confidence in the Lord than to put confidence in princes.
All the nations surrounded me; in the Lord’s name I resisted them.
They encircled me and surrounded me; in the Lord’s name I resisted them.
They surrounded me like bees around a honeycomb, and they blazed like fire among thorns; in the Lord’s name I resisted them.
I was shoved and was about to fall, but the Lord supported me.
The Lord is my strength and my song, and he has become my salvation.
The sound of joy and salvation is in the dwellings of the righteous. The Lord’s right hand has done mighty deeds.
The Lord’s right hand has lifted me up.
I will not die, but will live and tell of the Lord’s deeds.
The Lord [?] disciplined me, but he will not hand me over to death.
Open the gates of righteousness for me; I will enter through them and give thanks to the Lord.
This is the Lord’s gate; the righteous will enter through it.
I will give thanks to you because you heard me and became my salvation.
The stone that the builders [?] has become the cornerstone.
This came from the Lord, and it is wonderful in our eyes.
This is the day the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it.
O Lord, save us! O Lord, grant us success!
Blessed is the one who comes in the Lord’s name. We have given blessings from the Lord’s house.
The Lord is God, and he has shone upon us. Organize the festival of those who give shade, as far as the horns of the altar.
You are my God, and I will give thanks to you. You are my God, and I will exalt you. I will give thanks to you because you heard me and became my salvation.
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy lasts forever.
Glory. Sessional hymn. Alleluia.
Blessed are those who are blameless in their way, who walk in the law of the Lord.
Blessed are those who search his testimonies; they will seek him with their whole heart.
For those who do no wrong have walked in his ways.
You commanded that your commandments be kept diligently.
Oh, that my ways might be set straight, so that I may keep your statutes!
Then I will not be ashamed when I look upon all your commandments.
I will praise you with an upright heart when I learn your righteous judgments.
I will keep your statutes; do not utterly forsake me.
How can a young man set your way straight? By keeping your words.
With my whole heart I have sought you; do not cast me away from your commandments.
I have hidden your words in my heart, so that I may not sin against you.
Blessed are you, Lord; teach me your statutes.
With my lips I have declared all the judgments of your mouth.
I have delighted in the way of your testimonies as in all riches.
I will meditate on your commandments and understand your ways.
I will study your statutes and will not forget your words.
Reward your servant and give me life, and I will keep your words.
Open my eyes, and I will understand the wonders of your law.
I am a stranger on the earth; do not hide your commandments from me.
My soul has loved to long for your judgments at all times.
You have rebuked the proud; a curse is upon those who turn away from your commandments.
Take reproach and contempt away from me, for I have sought your testimonies.
For princes sat and spoke against me, but your servant bowed down in your statutes.
For your testimonies are my study, and my counsels are in your statutes.
My soul clings to the earth; give me life according to your word.
I declared my ways, and you heard me; teach me your statutes.
Teach me the way of your statutes, and I will meditate on your wonders.
My soul has fallen asleep from despondency; strengthen me through your words.
Remove the way of falsehood from me, and show me mercy through your law.
I have chosen the way of truth and have not forgotten your judgments.
I have clung to your testimonies; Lord, do not put me to shame.
I ran along the way of your commandments when you made my heart spacious.
Lay down for me as a law, Lord, the way of your statutes, and I will seek it continually.
Give me understanding, and I will examine your law and keep it with all my heart.
Guide me along the path of your commandments, for I have desired it.
Incline my heart toward your testimonies and not toward greed.
Turn my eyes away so that they do not see vanity; give me life in your way.
Confirm your word to your servant, so that I may fear you.
Take away from me the disgrace that I dreaded, for your commands, Lord, [?].
See, I have longed for your judgments; give me life through your righteousness.
May your mercy come upon me, Lord, and your salvation according to your word.
And I will give an answer to those who reproach me, for I have trusted in your words.
Do not take the word of truth entirely from my mouth, for I have placed my hope in your judgments.
And I will keep your law continually, forever and ever.
And I walked in a spacious place, for I sought your commandments.
And I spoke of your testimonies before kings and was not ashamed.
And I meditated on your commandments, which I loved greatly.
And I lifted my hands toward your commandments, which I loved, and meditated on your statutes.
Remember your word to your servant, through which you have given me hope.
This comforted me in my humiliation: your word gave me life.
The proud transgressed the law greatly, but I did not turn away from your law.
I remembered your judgments from of old, Lord, and was comforted.
Sorrow seized me because of sinners who abandon your law.
Your statutes were songs to me in the place where I lived as a stranger.
I remembered your name in the night, Lord, and kept your law.
This came to me because I sought your statutes.
You are my portion, Lord; I said that I would keep your law.
I prayed before your face with all my heart: have mercy on me according to your word.
I considered your ways and turned my feet toward your testimonies.
I prepared myself and was not troubled, so that I might keep your commandments.
The ropes of sinners entangled me, but I did not forget your law.
At midnight I rose to give thanks to you for your righteous judgments.
I am a companion of all who fear you and keep your commandments.
The earth is full of your mercy, Lord; teach me your (your) statutes.
Do good to your servant, Lord, according to your word.
Teach me your goodness, discipline, and understanding, for I have believed in your commandments.
Before I was humbled, I sinned; for this reason I have kept your word.
You are good, Lord; in your goodness teach me your statutes.
The injustice of the proud against me increased, but I will study your commandments with all my heart.
Their hearts curdled like milk, but I meditated on your law.
It is good for me that you have humbled me, so that I may learn your statutes.
The law of your mouth is better for me than thousands of pieces of gold and silver. Glory.
Your hands made me and fashioned me. Give me understanding, and I will learn your statutes.
Those who fear you will see me and rejoice, because I have put my hope in your words.
I know, Lord, that your judgments are righteous, and that you have humbled me in faithfulness.
Let your mercy comfort me, according to your word to your servant.
Let your compassion come to me, and I shall live, for your law is my meditation.
Let the proud be put to shame, for they have acted lawlessly against me; but I will meditate on your commandments.
Let those who fear you turn to me, along with those who know your testimonies.
Let my heart be blameless in your statutes, so that I may not be put to shame.
My soul longs desperately for your salvation; I have put my hope in your words.
My eyes have grown weary waiting for your word, saying, “When will you look upon me?”
For I have become like a wineskin in the frost, yet I have not forgotten your statutes.
How many are the days of your servant? When will you give judgment for me against those who persecute me?
Lawbreakers have told me idle tales, but these are not like your law, Lord.
All your commandments are truth. They have persecuted me unjustly; help me.
They nearly made an end of me on earth, but I did not forsake your commandments.
Give me life according to your mercy, and I will keep the testimonies of your mouth.
Forever, Lord, your word remains in heaven.
Your truth endures from generation to generation. The one who established the earth endures.
The day continues according to your ordinance, for all things serve you.
If your law had not been my meditation, I would have perished in my affliction.
I will never forget your statutes, for through them you have given me life.
I am yours; save me, for I have not forgotten your statutes.
Sinners lay in wait for me to destroy me, but I have considered your testimonies.
I have seen the limit of every perfection; your commandment is exceedingly broad.
How I have loved your law, Lord! It is my meditation all day long.
You have made me wiser than my enemies through your commandment, for it is mine forever.
I have gained more understanding than all my teachers, for the testimonies
I sought your [?].
I kept my feet from every evil, so that I might keep your testimonies.
I did not turn aside from your judgments, for you have laid down a law for me.
How sweet your words are to my throat, sweeter than honey to my mouth!
Through your commandments I gained understanding; therefore I hated every unjust path.
Your law is a lamp to my feet and a light to my paths.
I have sworn and resolved to keep your righteous judgments.
I have been greatly humbled, Lord; give me life according to your word.
Accept the freewill offerings of my mouth, Lord, and teach me your judgments.
My soul is always in your hands, and I have not forgotten your law.
Sinners will lay a snare for me, but I have not strayed from your commandments.
I have inherited your testimonies forever, for they are the joy of my heart.
Incline my heart to carry out your statutes forever, for a reward.
I hated lawbreakers, but I loved your law.
You are my helper and protector; I have placed my hope in your words.
Depart from me, evildoers who examine the law of my God.
Receive me according to your word, and I will live; do not put me to shame in my hope.
Help me, and I will be saved, and I will meditate on your statutes.
You have brought to nothing all who stray from your statutes, for their thinking is unjust.
I regarded all the sinners of the earth as transgressors; therefore I loved your law.
Nail my flesh with your [?], for I have feared your commandments.
I have done what is just and right; do not hand me over to those who wrong me.
Wait for your servant for good; do not let the proud slander me.
My eyes have grown weary looking for your salvation and for the word of your righteousness.
Deal with your servant according to your mercy; teach me your statutes.
I am your servant; give me understanding, and I will know your testimonies.
It is time for the Lord to act; your law has been broken.
Therefore I have loved your law more than gold and topaz.
Therefore I have guided myself by all your commandments; I have hated every unjust path.
Your testimonies are wonderful; therefore my soul has searched them.
The explanation of your words gives light and gives understanding to little children.
I opened my mouth and drew in breath, because I longed for your commandments. GLORY.
Look upon me and have mercy on me, according to your judgment toward those who love your [?].
Guide my steps according to your word, and let no lawlessness rule over me.
Deliver me from human slander, and I will keep your commandments.
Let your face shine upon your servant, and teach me your statutes.
My eyes have poured out streams of water because I have not kept your law.
You are righteous, Lord, and your judgments are right.
You have commanded your testimonies in righteousness and complete truth.
Zeal for you has consumed me, because my enemies have forgotten your words.
Your word has been thoroughly refined by fire, and your servant has loved it.
I am young and despised, but I have not forgotten your statutes.
Your righteousness is righteousness forever, and your law is truth.
Afflictions and troubles have found me; your commandments are my meditation.
Your testimonies are righteous forever; give me understanding, and I will live.
I cried out with all my heart; hear me, Lord. I will seek your statutes.
I cried out to you: save me, and I will keep your testimonies.
I rose before dawn and cried out; I placed my hope in your words.
My eyes were awake before morning, so that I could meditate on your words.
Hear my voice, Lord, according to your mercy, and give me life according to your judgment.
The lawless people who persecute me have drawn near, but they have gone far from your law.
You are near, Lord, and all your ways are truth.
From the beginning I knew from your testimonies that you had established them forever.
See my lowliness and rescue me, for I have not forgotten your law.
Judge my case and deliver me; give me life for the sake of your word.
Salvation is far from sinners, because they have not sought your decrees.
Your mercies are many, Lord; give me life according to your judgment.
Many persecute and afflict me, but I have not turned away from your testimonies.
I saw those who lacked understanding and wasted away, because they did not keep your words.
See how I have loved your commandments; Lord, give me life through your mercy.
The beginning of your words is truth, and all your righteous judgments last forever.
Princes persecuted me [?], and my heart was afraid of your words.
I rejoice in your words like someone finding great spoils.
I have hated injustice, and it is hateful to me, but I have loved your law.
Seven times a day I praised you for your righteous judgments.
Those who love your law have great peace, and nothing makes them stumble.
I waited for your salvation, Lord, and I have loved your commandments.
My soul has kept your testimonies and loved them greatly.
I have kept your commandments and your testimonies, for all my ways are before you, Lord.
Let my prayer draw near before you, Lord; give me understanding according to your word.
Let my plea come before you, Lord; deliver me according to your word.
My lips will pour out a song of praise when you teach me your decrees.
My tongue will proclaim your words, for all your commandments are righteousness.
Let your hand save me, for I have loved your commandments.
I have loved your salvation, Lord, and your law is my meditation.
My soul will live and praise you, and your judgments will help me.
I have strayed like a lost sheep. Seek out your servant, for I have not forgotten your commandments.
Glory. [?] 3. A Song of Ascents.
When I was in distress, I cried out to the Lord, and he heard me.
Lord, deliver my soul from unrighteous lips and from a deceitful tongue.
What will be given to you, and what more will be added to you for your deceitful tongue?
The sharpened arrows of a mighty man, with burning coals (coals) from the wilderness.
Woe to me, for my stay in a foreign land has grown long! I have settled in dark tents.
My soul has lived long in a foreign land.
I was peaceful with those who hate peace. When I spoke to them, they fought against me [?].
A Song of Ascents.
I lifted my eyes to the mountain, from where my [?] will come.
My help comes from the Lord, who made heaven and earth.
Do not let your foot slip, and may he who guards you not slumber.
Look, he who guards Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.
The Lord will guard you; the Lord is your shelter at your right hand.
The sun will not burn you by day, nor the moon by night.
The Lord will guard you from every evil; the Lord will guard your soul.
The Lord will guard your coming in and your going out, from now and forever.
A Song of Ascents.
I rejoiced at those who said to me, “Let us go to the house of the Lord.”
Our feet were standing in your courts, Jerusalem.
Jerusalem is being built as a city whose community is joined together.
For there the tribes of the Lord will go up, as a testimony for Israel, to give thanks to the name of the Lord.
For there thrones will be set for judgment, thrones in the house of David.
Pray for the peace of Jerusalem and prosperity for those who love you.
May there be peace within your strength and prosperity within your fortified walls.
For the sake of my brothers and my neighbors, I spoke peace to you.
For the sake of the house of the Lord our God, I sought your good.
Song of Ascents.
I lifted my eyes to you, who dwell in heaven.
See, as the eyes of servants look to the hands of their masters, as the eyes of a maidservant look to the hand of her mistress, so our eyes look to the Lord our God until he has mercy on us.
Have mercy on us, Lord, have mercy on us, for we have been filled with contempt.
Our soul has been filled to overflowing with the scorn of the prosperous and the contempt of the proud.
Song of Ascents.
If the Lord had not been with us—let Israel now say—
if the Lord had not been with us when people rose up against us,
then they would have swallowed us alive when his anger raged against us.
Then the water would have drowned us; our soul passed through the torrent.
Then our soul passed through overwhelming waters.
Blessed is the Lord, who did not give us as prey to their teeth.
Our soul escaped like a bird from the hunters’ snare. The snare was broken, and we were delivered.
Our help is in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth.
Glory. Song of Ascents.
Those who trust in the Lord are like Mount Zion; the one who lives in Jerusalem will never be shaken.
Mountains surround it, and the Lord surrounds his people, from now and forever.
For the Lord will not leave the scepter of sinners over the allotted land of the righteous, so that the righteous may not stretch out their hands to do evil.
Do good, Lord, to the good and to those who are upright in heart.
But those who turn aside into crooked ways the Lord will lead away with those who practice lawlessness. Peace be upon Israel.
Song of Ascents.
When the Lord brought back the captives of Zion, we were like those who are comforted.
Then our mouths were filled with joy, and our tongues with gladness. Then they will say among the nations, “The Lord has done great things with us.”
The Lord has done great things with us; we were glad.
Bring back our captives, Lord, like streams in the south.
Those who sowed in tears will reap in joy.
They went on their way and wept as they scattered their seed, but they will surely return with joy, carrying their sheaves.
A song of ascents.
Unless the Lord builds the house, those who build it labor in vain. Unless the Lord guards the city, the watchman stays awake in vain.
It is in vain for you to rise early. Rise after sitting down, you who eat the bread of pain, when he gives sleep to his own beloved.
Look, sons are the Lord’s inheritance; the fruit of your womb is a reward.
Like arrows in the hand of a mighty man, so are the sons of those who were driven out.
Blessed is the man who fulfills his desire with them. They will not be put to shame when they speak to their enemies at the gates.
A song of ascents.
Blessed are all who fear the Lord, who walk in his ways.
You will eat the fruit of your own labor. You are blessed, and it will go well with you.
Your wife is like a fruitful vine within your house; your sons are like young olive shoots around your table.
Look, this is how the person who fears the Lord will be blessed.
May the Lord bless you from Zion, and may you see good things in Jerusalem all the days of my life.
And you will see your sons’ sons. Peace (peace) upon Israel.
A song of ascents.
Many times they fought against me from my youth—let Israel now say—
Many times they fought against me from my youth, but they did not prevail against me.
Sinners hammered on my back; they prolonged their lawlessness.
The Lord is righteous; he cut through the necks of sinners.
May all who hate Zion be put to shame and turn back.
Let them be like grass on the rooftops, which withers before it is pulled up.
With it the reaper does not fill his hand, nor does the gatherer of sheaves fill his lap.
And those passing by did not say, “The blessing of the Lord be upon you! We have blessed you in the name of the Lord.”
Glory. A Song of Ascents.
Out of the depths I cried to you, Lord.
Lord, hear my voice. Let your ears attend to the voice of my prayer.
If you keep watch over my lawless deeds, Lord, Lord, who will stand?
For forgiveness comes from you.
For your name’s sake ([?]) I waited for you, Lord. My soul waited for your word.
Let Israel hope in the Lord. From the morning watch until night; from the morning watch let Israel hope in the Lord.
For mercy comes from the Lord, and abundant redemption comes from him.
And he will redeem Israel from all his lawless deeds.
A Song of Ascents.
Lord, my heart was not proud, nor were my eyes raised high. I did not pursue great things, or wonders beyond me.
If I did not humble myself, but exalted my soul, like a weaned child toward its mother, so will you repay my soul.
Let Israel hope in the Lord, from now and forever.
A Song of Ascents.
Lord, remember David and all his gentleness.
How he swore to the Lord and made a vow to the God of Jacob:
“If I enter the dwelling of my house, or climb onto the bed where I lie;
if I give sleep to my eyes, slumber to my eyelids, or rest to my temples,
until I find a place for the Lord, a dwelling for the God of Jacob.”
Look, we heard of it in Ephrathah and found it in the wooded fields.
Let us enter his dwellings and bow down at the place where his feet stood.
Arise, Lord, into your resting place, you [?] the ark of your holiness.
Your priests will clothe themselves in righteousness, and your holy ones will rejoice with joy.
For the sake of David your servant, do not turn away the face of your anointed one.
The Lord swore to David in truth, and he will not go back on it: “I will set those born from your womb on your throne.
If your sons keep my covenant and these decrees that I will teach them, his sons too will sit on your throne forever.”
For the Lord chose Zion; he desired it as his dwelling place.
“This is my resting place forever (forever) and ever; here I will dwell, for I have desired it.
I will surely bless his widow; I will satisfy the poor man with bread.
His priests will clothe themselves in salvation, and his holy ones will rejoice with joy.
There I will make David’s horn grow; I will prepare a lamp for my anointed one.
I will clothe his enemies in shame, but upon him my holiness will blossom.”
Psalm. Song of ascents. [?]
See how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to live together!
It is like anointing oil on the head, running down onto Aaron’s beard, Aaron’s beard, running down onto the edges of his robe.
It is like the dew of Hermon descending onto the mountains of Zion, for there the Lord commanded blessing and life forever.
Psalm. Song of ascents.
Now bless the Lord, all you servants of the Lord who stand in the Lord’s temple and in the courts of the house of our God.
At night lift up your hands toward the sanctuary and bless the Lord.
May the Lord, who made heaven and earth, bless you from Zion.
Glory. [?]. Alleluia.
Praise the name of the Lord; praise him, you servants of the Lord,
who stand in the Lord’s temple, in the courts of the house of our God.
Praise the Lord, for the Lord is good; sing to his name, for it is pleasant.
For the Lord chose Jacob for himself, Israel as his own possession.
For I know that the Lord is great, and our God is above all [?].
Everything he wished, he did in heaven and on earth, in the sea and in all the depths.
He raises clouds from the ends of the earth; he makes lightning for the rain.
He struck down every firstborn in Egypt, from humans to livestock.
He sent signs and wonders into your midst, Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his servants.
He struck down many nations and killed mighty kings:
Sihon, king of the Amorites, and Og, king of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Canaan.
And he gave the land to them as an inheritance, to his people.
Lord, your name endures forever, and your remembrance from generation to generation.
For the Lord will judge his people and have compassion on his servants.
The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of human hands.
They have mouths but do not speak; they have eyes but do not see.
They have ears but do not hear, for there is no breath in their mouths.
May those who make them become like them, and all who trust in them.
House of Israel, bless the Lord! House of Aaron, bless the Lord!
House of Levi, bless the Lord! You who fear the Lord, bless the Lord!
Blessed be the Lord from Zion, who dwells in Jerusalem!
Hallelujah!
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
Give thanks to the God of gods, for his mercy endures forever.
Give thanks to the Lord of lords, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
To him who alone does great wonders, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
To him who established the earth upon the waters, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
To him who alone made the great lights, for his mercy endures forever.
The moon and stars to rule the night, for his mercy endures forever.
To him who struck down Egypt's firstborn, for his mercy endures forever.
To him who brought Israel out from [?] them, for (for) his mercy endures forever.
With a strong hand and an uplifted arm, for his mercy endures forever.
To him who divided the Red Sea into parts, for his mercy [?].
And led Israel out from its midst, for his mercy endures forever.
To him who shook Pharaoh and his army into the Red Sea, for mercy endures forever.
To him who led his people into the wilderness, for his mercy endures forever.
To him who struck down great kings, for [?] forever.
And to him who killed mighty kings, for his mercy endures forever.
Sihon, king of the Amorites, for his mercy endures forever.
And Og, king of Bashan, for mercy endures forever.
And to him who gave their land as an inheritance, for his mercy endures forever.
An inheritance to Israel his servant, for his mercy endures forever.
For the Lord remembered us in our lowliness, for mercy endures forever.
He has delivered us from our enemies, for his mercy endures forever.
He gives food to all flesh, for his mercy endures forever.
Give thanks to the God of heaven, for mercy endures forever.
A PSALM OF DAVID.
By the river of Babylon, there we sat and wept as we remembered Zion.
On the willows in its midst we hung our instruments.
And there those who had taken us captive asked us for the words of songs, and those who had led us away asked for singing: “Sing us some songs of Zion.”
How shall we sing the Lord’s song in a foreign land?
If I forget you, Jerusalem, let my right hand be forgotten.
May my tongue cling to my throat if I do not remember you, if I do not put Jerusalem first among my joys.
Remember, Lord, the sons of Edom on the day of Jerusalem [?], who said, “Raze it, raze it (to the foundation), to its foundations!”
Wretched daughter of Babylon, blessed is he who repays you with the repayment you gave.
GLORY. AND ZECHARIAH’S GLORY, TWO [?].
I will give thanks to you, Lord, with all my heart, and before the angels I will sing to you, because you have heard all the words of my mouth.
I will bow down toward your holy temple. I will give thanks to your name for your mercy and your truth, because you have exalted the holy name above all things.
On whatever day I call upon you, you will hear me and increase the strength in my soul.
Let all the kings of the earth give thanks to you, Lord, because they have heard all the words of your mouth.
They will sing the Lord’s songs, because great is the glory of the Lord.
For the Lord is high, yet he looks upon the humble, and he knows the proud from far away.
If you give me life in the midst of trouble, you will stretch out your hand against the anger of my enemies, and your right hand will save me.
The Lord will act on my behalf. Lord, your mercy lasts forever; do not disregard the works of your hands.
A PSALM OF DAVID.
Lord, you have examined me and known me.
You know when I sit down and when I rise. You understand my thoughts from far away.
You have searched out my path and my untrodden way; you have looked over all my ways.
For there is no deceit on my tongue.
Look, Lord, you know everything, the latest and the earliest. You formed me and laid your hand (on [?]) on me.
Your knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is beyond my strength, and I cannot attain [?].
Where shall I go from your Spirit, and where shall I flee from your presence?
If I ascend to heaven, you are there. If I descend into Hades, you are there.
If I take up my wings at dawn and settle in the farthest places, in darkness [?],
even there your hand will guide me, and your right hand will hold me.
And I said, “Surely darkness will overwhelm me, and the night will be light for those who cry out [?].”
Even darkness is not dark before you, and the night will shine like the day. Its darkness is like its light.
For you formed my inward parts, and from my mother’s womb [?].
I will give thanks to you, because you have shown yourself fearfully wonderful. Your works are wonders, and my soul knows this very well.
My bone was not hidden from you, which you made in secret, nor my substance in the depths of the earth.
Your eyes saw my unformed body, and in your books they will all be written. In a day they will not be formed, and there is no one among them [?].
Your friends have been very precious to me, O God; their authority has grown exceedingly strong [?].
I will count them: they will be more numerous than the sand. I awoke, and I am still with you.
If you kill the sinner, O God—men of blood, turn away from me!
For he said in his thoughts, “They will take their own cities in vain.”
Have I not hated those who hate you, Lord, and wasted away over enemies?
I have hated them with complete hatred; they have become my enemies.
Test me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me, and I shall know my paths.
And see whether there is a lawless way in me, and guide me on the everlasting way.
For the end. A psalm of David.
Rescue me, Lord, from an evil person; deliver me from an unjust man.
They devised injustice in their hearts and prepared battles all day long.
They sharpened their tongues like a serpent’s, and the venom of an asp is under their lips.
Protect me, Lord, from the hand of the sinner; rescue me from the unjust man—from those who planned to trip my feet.
The proud hid a net for me, and with ropes they stretched a net for my feet. Beside the path they laid a stumbling block for me.
I said to the Lord, “You are my God.” Listen, Lord, to the voice of my prayer.
Lord, Lord, strength of my salvation, he has sheltered my head on the day of battle.
Do not hand me over to a sinner, Lord, because of my own desire. They have plotted against me. Do not abandon me, lest he exalt himself.
The head of their surrounding band—the trouble from their lips will cover them.
Coals of fire will fall upon them. You will cast them down into sufferings, and they will not stand.
A man of many words will not prosper on earth; evil will hear the unjust man, to his destruction.
I know that the Lord will give justice to the needy and vindication to the poor.
Nevertheless, the righteous will give thanks to your name, and the righteous will rejoice; they will give thanks to your name.
Glory. A psalm of David.
Lord, I have cried out to you; hear me. Attend to the voice of my prayer when I cry out to you.
Let my prayer rise like incense before you, and the lifting of my hands like the evening sacrifice.
Set a guard over my mouth, Lord, and a protective door over my lips.
Do not turn my heart toward deceitful words, to devise [?] in sins with people who practice lawlessness; and let them not join with their chosen ones.
A righteous man will teach me through his mercy and rebuke me, but let the oil of sinners not anoint my head. For my prayer is still for favor.
Their judges were swallowed up beside the rock. My words will be heard, for I shall prevail.
As a clod of earth is broken apart upon the ground, their bones were scattered beside Hades.
For my eyes are turned toward you, Lord, Lord; they have placed their hope in you. Do not take away my soul.
Keep me from this net that they have set for me, from the snares of those who practice lawlessness.
Sinners will fall into their own net. I am alone until I pass through.
A contemplation. Of David. A prayer when he was in the cave.
With my voice I cried out to the Lord; with my voice I prayed to the Lord.
I will pour out my prayer before him and declare my sorrow before him.
When my spirit was failing within me, he knew my paths. On this road along which I walked, they hid snares for me.
I looked to my right and watched, but there was no one who knew me. Escape failed me, and there was no one who sought my soul.
I cried out to you, Lord. I said, “You are my hope, and you are my portion in the land of the living.”
Listen to my prayer, for I have been brought very low. Deliver me from those who pursue me, for they have become stronger than I.
Bring my soul out of prison, so that I may give thanks to your name. Sinners are waiting for me until you repay me.
A psalm. Of David.
Lord, hear my prayer; listen to my plea in your truth. Hear me in your righteousness.
And do not enter into judgment with your servant, for no one living will be justified before you.
For the enemy has pursued my soul and brought my life down to the ground. He has made me dwell in dark places, like those long dead.
My spirit grew faint within me; my heart was troubled within me.
I remembered the days of old. I meditated on all your deeds and reflected on the works of your hands.
I stretched out my hands toward you; my soul is like waterless land before you.
Hear me quickly, Lord; my spirit is failing. Do not turn your face away from me, or I shall become like those who go down into the pit.
Let me hear of your mercy in the morning, for I have placed my hope in you. Show me, Lord, the way I should go, for I have lifted up my soul to you.
Rescue me from my enemies, Lord; I have taken refuge in you.
Teach me to do your will, for you are my God. Your good Spirit will guide me on level ground.
For your name’s sake, Lord, you will give me life; in your righteousness you will bring my soul out of [?].
In your mercy you will destroy my enemies and put an end to all who oppress my soul, for I am your servant.
Glory. [?]
Blessed is the Lord God, and [?], who trains my hands for battle and my fingers for war.
My mercy and my refuge, my defender and my deliverer, my protector in whom I have trusted, who subjects my people to me.
Lord, what is a human being that you have made yourself known to him, or a son of man that you heed him, that you take account of him?
Man has become like [?]; his days pass like [?].
Lord, bend [?] the heavens and come down; as he came down, the mountains will smoke.
Flash forth lightning and you will scatter them; send out your arrows and you will throw them into confusion.
Send your hand from above; rescue me and deliver me from the many waters and from the hand of foreigners.
Their mouths have spoken [?], and their right hand is a right hand of unrighteousness.
God, I will sing a new song [?] to you; on a ten-stringed harp I will sing to you.
To you who give salvation to kings, who deliver David your servant from a cruel weapon [?].
Deliver me and rescue me from the hand [?] of foreigners, whose mouths speak falsehood and whose right hand is a right hand of unrighteousness.
Their sons are like young shoots, firmly established in their youth; their daughters are adorned and fashioned like [?] of a temple.
Their storehouses [?] are full, pouring out from [?] into [?]; their sheep are numerous [?] and multiply in their pastures [?].
Their oxen are fat. There is no miscarriage, no going out, and no outcry in their streets [?].
People have called those who have these things blessed. Blessed are the people whose God is the Lord.
Psalm. Of David.
I will exalt you, my God, King [?], and bless your name for [?].
Every day I will bless you [?] and praise your name forever.
You are [?], greatly praised, and there is no end to his greatness [?].
Generation after generation will praise your works and proclaim [?] your power.
They will speak of the splendor of the glory of holiness [?], and proclaim your wonders.
They will tell of the power of your fearsome deeds and proclaim your greatness.
They will pour forth the memory of your abundant goodness and rejoice in your righteousness.
The Lord is compassionate and merciful, patient and very merciful.
The Lord is good to all, and his [?] is over all his works.
All your works will give thanks to you, Lord, and your holy ones will bless themselves.
They will speak of the glory of your kingdom and tell of your power,
to make your power known to human beings, and the glory of the splendor of your kingdom.
Your kingdom is a kingdom for all ages, a dominion throughout every generation. The Lord is faithful in every word and holy in all his works.
The Lord supports all who are falling and raises up all who have been cast down.
The eyes of all look to you in hope, and you give them food at the proper time.
You open your hand and satisfy every living creature with your favor.
The Lord is righteous in all his ways and holy in all his works.
The Lord is near to all who call upon him, to all who call upon him in truth.
He will fulfill the will of those who fear him; he will hear their prayer and save them. [?]
The Lord guards all who love him, and he will destroy all sinners.
My mouth will speak the praise of the Lord, and let all flesh bless his holy name forever and ever.
GLORY. ALLELUIA. OF ZECHARIAH.
Praise the Lord, my soul.
I will praise the Lord throughout my life; I sing to my God as long as I exist.
Do not put your trust in princes or in human beings, in whom there is no salvation.
His spirit will depart; he will return to [?]. On that day all their thoughts will perish.
Their blessedness [?]. His hope is in the Lord his God,
who made heaven and earth, the sea and everything that exists; who keeps truth forever
and brings justice to those who have been wronged, who gives food to the hungry. The Lord sets prisoners free.
The Lord gives wisdom to the blind; the Lord raises up those who have been cast down; the Lord loves the righteous.
The Lord protects strangers. He takes in the orphan and the widow, but destroys the way of sinners.
The Lord will reign forever, your God, Zion, from generation to generation.
Alleluia. Zechariah.
Praise the Lord, for a psalm is good; may our God delight in praise.
The Lord builds Jerusalem; he will gather the scattered people of Israel.
He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.
He counts the multitude of stars and gives names to them all.
Great is our Lord, and great is his strength; his understanding is beyond measure.
The Lord supports the meek; he [?] sinners down to the ground.
Begin with thanksgiving to the Lord; sing to our God with harps.
He covers the sky with clouds, prepares rain for the earth, makes grass grow on the mountains, and plants for human use.
He gives food to [?], and to all the young ravens [?] that cry out.
He does not delight in the strength of a horse, nor does he take pleasure in the deceits of men.
